sections.heading: What should the brief say if my child is in MYP rather than DP?
paragraphs: Say the year and the criteria that are being missed, not just the subject. For the Middle Years Programme (MYP) a useful brief reads something like: MYP 4, Sciences, scoring consistently lower on criterion B and C than on A. That single line tells us to look for somebody who teaches investigation design and analysis rather than content revision, and it will produce a different shortlist from Year 9 Science, needs help. The criteria are the assessment, so they belong in the brief.

For the Diploma Programme (DP) the brief needs the level and the component. Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), which paper is weak, and whether the Internal Assessment (IA) has been started. A DP 2 student whose written papers are solid but whose IA draft has not moved since October needs a tutor who can supervise coursework, which is a different skill from exam teaching and a different conversation about hours. If the Extended Essay (EE) or Theory of Knowledge (TOK) is the real problem, say that outright, because very few tutors are genuinely good at both TOK and a subject.

For IGCSE, tell us the board and the tier. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, and Core and Extended are different courses in practice. A student entered for Extended who is being taught as though Core will be fine is a common and fixable problem, and spotting it is often worth more than a term of tutoring. For the Primary Years Programme (PYP) the brief is simplest of all: describe what the child avoids doing rather than what they score, because PYP reporting is not built for grade comparisons.

Whatever the programme, we take the structure of components from the live subject guide and the school coordinator rather than from memory. Boards revise their guides on their own cycles, so the honest position for anyone arranging home tuition in Mumbai is to name the skills a tutor should be building and to send parents to the current guide for anything that looks like a weighting or a word count.

sections.heading: Several subjects at once: how we sequence a multi-subject request
paragraphs: We sequence rather than supply everything on day one, and parents sometimes find that irritating until the second month. A request covering four subjects usually becomes one tutor for the worst one and a review date four weeks out. The reason is that study habits transfer: a student who learns to annotate a question properly in Economics starts doing it in Geography without anybody being paid to teach that. Booking all four immediately means paying four tutors to teach the same transferable habit while the student does progressively less work alone.

Where two tutors are genuinely needed, we split by group rather than by convenience. Mathematics and Physics sit together comfortably with one person. Chemistry and Economics do not, and a tutor who offers both to the same child is teaching one properly. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Worli Sea Face covers, the pattern that works is two specialists on separate evenings rather than one generalist four times a week, even though it is more work for us to arrange and slightly more expensive for you.

The subjects that fill quickly on the island are Mathematics, the three sciences, Economics, Business Management and English A. The ones that take longer are specific Standard Level languages, Design Technology, Music and Visual Arts, and the more unusual Group 3 options. If your child needs one of the slower ones, ask early in the academic year. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents hope to find in one person is a bench of specialists, and some rows on that bench are thin.

There is one sequencing exception. When an internal assessment or coursework deadline is close, we will put a second tutor in immediately, because coursework does not wait for habits to transfer. A DP 2 student with a stalled investigation write-up and a mock fortnight approaching needs two people for six weeks and then one. We will say when that applies and when it does not, rather than treating every deadline as an emergency.

sections.heading: Should the first four home classes be at the table or on a screen?
paragraphs: At the table, if the option exists. The first four sessions are where a tutor learns the things that never appear on a video call: how long the student works before looking away, whether anything gets written down before an answer is spoken, whether the study space is a desk or a corner of a sofa with the television on. Those four sessions set the plan for the term, and a plan built on partial information gets rewritten in week six.

After that, the mode can relax. Online genuinely earns its place in three situations and we recommend it in all of them. A subject nobody local teaches well. A tutor who is the right person but lives in another city. And short, frequent contact: twenty minutes twice a week on a draft, which is easy on a screen and impossible to justify as a house visit. Older DP 2 students who are already organised often prefer online and lose almost nothing by it.

Hybrid is where most of our year-long arrangements end up, and it works better when chosen in September than when stumbled into in January. One substantial session in the flat carries the teaching; one short midweek call handles the draft, the question from Wednesday's class and the thing the student did not want to ask in front of a parent. Decide which of the two is immovable, because the movable one will be moved repeatedly.

The trade-offs, stated without spin: online requires a tablet and stylus at both ends or the written working vanishes from the lesson, and a student who avoids difficulty finds a screen a very comfortable place to avoid it. In-person costs travel time, which shows up in the fee and caps how many slots a tutor can offer on one evening. For most families on the sea face the in-person cost is worth paying for the first term and optional after that.

sections.heading: How is an IB home tutor in Mumbai verified before you see the profile?
paragraphs: Three checks, all completed before the profile leaves our side. Identity against a government photo document. The qualification that backs each subject claim, seen rather than described. And teaching history confirmed with somebody who has watched the person teach, which is the check that removes the most candidates. If a tutor claims examining or moderating experience for a board, we ask for evidence and strike the claim from the profile if none arrives. A profile you receive has had the easy exaggerations taken out of it.

We are also careful about what goes on the profile in the other direction. You get subjects, levels, boards, years of experience and availability. You do not get the tutor's address, phone number or employer until you have both agreed to proceed, which protects them as much as it protects you. Parents occasionally ask for a photograph of the identity document; we do not forward those, and a service that does is being careless with somebody.

What verification cannot cover is the part that decides the outcome. We cannot verify patience, we cannot verify how a tutor behaves in a week when a student is rude, and we cannot predict whether a particular adult and a particular fifteen-year-old will get along. That is what the discovery call and the four week review are for, and it is why a free swap exists rather than being presented as a concession. Treat a verified profile as a statement that the facts are true, not that the match will work.

Your own checks take ten minutes and are worth more than ours. Ask which board and syllabus year the tutor last taught this course in. Ask what their previous student in it was getting wrong. Ask what they will refuse to teach. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or quotes a pass rate, because neither is something an honest tutor has. And get the weekly slot and the review cadence in writing, which any serious person supplies without being pressed.

sections.heading: What actually happens on the free discovery call?
paragraphs: Twenty minutes, no charge, and the student should be on it even if they would rather not be. The call has three parts. The tutor asks the student something specific about recent work, usually with a paper or a draft in front of them. The parent asks about board experience, reporting and availability. Then everybody decides whether to proceed, and nobody is expected to decide on the call itself. There is no sales stage, because the tutor is not paying us a commission for closing you.

The part worth paying attention to is the first few minutes, when the tutor talks to your child rather than about them. A strong tutor asks a question your child can half answer and then asks why, and keeps going until the gap is visible. A weak one explains how they teach. If your child says three sentences in twenty minutes because the adults filled the space, that is information about the adults, and it is a reason to let the second call run differently.

Parents frequently ask what they should say. Say the awkward things. That the last tutor did not work out and why. That your son has stopped doing homework rather than finding it hard. That you are not sure you can protect the 7pm slot once football restarts. A tutor who hears all of that on the call plans for it; a tutor who hears it in week five has already built the wrong plan. We would rather lose a placement on an honest call than fill one on an optimistic one.

If both shortlisted tutors seem equally good, ask us which we would pick. We will answer, and the answer is usually about schedule stability rather than brilliance: whoever lives closest, has the fewest new students this term and already holds a pass for a neighbouring tower. That is the unglamorous arithmetic behind most durable IB Gram home tuition in Worli Sea Face arrangements, and it beats a marginally stronger tutor who will be rescheduling by November.

sections.heading: When things go wrong: missed sessions, exam season and honest limits
paragraphs: Missed sessions are the most common failure and the easiest to fix. The pattern is almost always the same: a slot chosen optimistically, a tutor arriving late twice, a cancellation on a Monday that is never rescheduled, and a quiet drift by week seven. The fix is procedural rather than moral. Pick a time you can defend, agree in advance what happens to a cancelled session, and tell us when two slip in a row rather than waiting to see if it settles. It does not settle.

Exam season is the second predictable problem. In the weeks before mocks, every family wants more hours from the same tutor, and a tutor with five students in one cohort cannot give all five an extra session. We spread tutors across programmes and schools partly for this reason, but the honest answer is that extra hours in March are a lottery and extra hours in September are not. Families who start early effectively buy insurance against this.

The third is a tutor who has to stop mid-term. It happens: people move, change jobs, or take on something that clashes. We handle the replacement, we ask the outgoing tutor for a written handover of what has been covered and what is still weak, and we try to give you a profile within the week. A handover note is the difference between a new tutor starting from scratch and starting from where your child actually is, and it is one of the few genuine advantages of going through a platform at all.

The honest limits are worth stating plainly. We do not guarantee grades, we publish no success rates, and we will not promise a number of weeks to fix a problem, because the variables outside anybody's control are large: sleep, subject load, how fully the school's teaching covers the syllabus, and whether the student wants this. What we will commit to is verified profiles, a free call before you spend anything, a written review every two to four weeks, a replacement on request, and a straight no when we cannot help.

sections.heading: Which boards, years and levels does IB Gram cover in Worli?
paragraphs: Both the International Baccalaureate (IB) and IGCSE, across roughly Years 1 to 12, which is what the schools around Worli actually run. On the IB side that means the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through the middle school with its criterion marking, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years with Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) choices, Internal Assessment (IA) components in every subject, the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK). On the IGCSE side that means Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses, with Core and Extended tiers where the subject offers them.

Coverage is not uniform and pretending otherwise would waste your time. Depth is strongest where Mumbai demand is heaviest: DP mathematics and the three sciences, MYP mathematics and sciences, IGCSE mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology, and English across both boards. It thins at the edges, which in practice means DP Higher Level music or film, a less common Language B, some Group 3 options at HL, and PYP support for a child in an early year, where what a family often needs is not a subject tutor at all. Where the pool is thin for an in-person match we say so rather than sending a generalist and hoping.

The level is the part parents under-specify most. IB Gram home tuition in Worli for a Year 11 IGCSE candidate and for a DP Year 2 candidate are different services with different tutors, even in the same subject, because the assessment logic differs: tiered papers with command words on one side, externally examined papers plus a moderated internal component on the other. When you write to us, name the level and the year together, and name the exam session your child is sitting if they are in an examination year. That single line removes a round of back and forth and often changes the shortlist entirely.

sections.heading: Subject coverage, and the honest limits of it
paragraphs: A tutor covering all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Worli breadth does not exist, and the profiles we send are deliberately narrow. A DP Physics HL specialist will usually also handle IGCSE physics and MYP sciences, because the subject spine is continuous. The same person is not the right choice for DP Economics, and we do not pretend they are. Where a family needs two subjects, the usual arrangement is two tutors on two evenings, or one tutor in person plus one online for the scarcer subject, which in Worli is workable because the tutor pool here is relatively deep. Most of the home tuition we arrange in Mumbai is single-subject for exactly this reason.

What a specialist actually brings is knowledge of where marks are lost, which is subject-specific in ways that surprise parents. In the DP sciences the internally assessed investigation is marked against its own criteria and students lose ground on method and evaluation rather than on chemistry or physics. In DP mathematics the exploration rewards a genuine personal line of enquiry and punishes a textbook topic restated. In the IGCSE sciences the alternative-to-practical paper tests whether a student can describe a method, control a variable and read an instrument precisely, none of which appears in a theory revision guide. English across both boards rewards argument about how a text is constructed and penalises retelling.

So when you ask about subject coverage, ask about component coverage. Has this tutor supervised an exploration or an investigation before? Have they prepared candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper? Have they marked a commentary portfolio? For MYP, have they judged work against criteria A to D in that subject group? Those questions sort a specialist from a confident graduate faster than any qualification check, and they are exactly what we ask a tutor before listing them. If you are also weighing up IB tuition fees in Worli, component experience is the single factor most likely to justify a higher rate honestly.

The route is set by travel arithmetic rather than by distance. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow, and a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres while still losing up to forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. Which is why tutors here are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, and why a tutor who already has two Worli families will take you on readily while a tutor whose other students are in Andheri will not, however good they look on paper.

Worli breaks that rule in one direction only, and it is the single most useful fact about tutoring here. The Sea Link ramp at the northern end means a Bandra-based specialist reaches Worli in roughly fifteen minutes off-peak, which makes Worli the most commonly accepted cross-harbour match in the city. No other locality on the island gets that. In practice it means the Worli shortlist for a scarce HL subject has Bandra and Khar names on it that a Cuffe Parade shortlist would not, and it is why IB Gram home classes in Worli can often be arranged in person where the same request further south becomes an online one. sections.heading: How the Mumbai school year shapes an IB Gram schedule
paragraphs: We schedule against the school calendar, not against a twelve-month contract, which is one reason there is no lock-in. Families in Worli attend Ryan Global School, which has a Worli campus, Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo and JBCN International School, Parel, among others across Mumbai. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of those schools or with any examination board. We name them because their term dates and internal deadlines determine when a tutor is useful and when the same hours are wasted.

The year has a rhythm every tutor here recognises. June and July are open: capacity exists, rates are negotiable in the honest sense that a tutor with free hours is more flexible, and the work can be diagnostic rather than reactive. From late August the first assessments land. October is report season and the heaviest week of inbound requests we get, which also means the strongest specialists are committing their last slots. November and December stack DP Internal Assessment drafts against IGCSE coursework deadlines. January is mocks. February and March are revision, and demand shifts from weekly teaching to short intensive blocks. The May examination session then empties the calendar again.

What this means for a Worli family is practical. If you want a specific tutor at a specific hour, ask in the quiet months. If you are asking in late October, be flexible on the day or the format and you will still get a good match; insist on 7pm on Wednesday and you will get whoever is left. During mock and revision season we often restructure a booking from ninety minutes weekly to two shorter sessions, because that matches how revision actually works, and the home classes we run in Mumbai through February are shorter and more frequent than the ones we run in July. An IB tutor Mumbai families keep across two academic years is almost always one whose schedule was built around the school's calendar from the start.

sections.heading: Does IB Gram home tuition in Worli ever move online?
paragraphs: Yes, and we would rather tell you when than discover it mid-term. Home tutoring is the lead service and the default: a tutor at your table sees the working, holds a teenager's attention better, and can mark a past paper with a pen in hand. For younger students and for anyone whose problem is partly motivation, that physical presence is most of the value. IB Gram home tuition in Worli is arranged in person wherever the subject, the level and your hour allow it, and in Worli that is more often than in most of South Mumbai because of the pool the Sea Link opens up.

Four situations move a booking online, temporarily or permanently. Scarcity: if the right specialist for DP Economics HL or a Language B oral is not reachable at your hour, an IB online tutor in Worli beats a local generalist every time, and we will say so plainly. Weather: monsoon weeks break in-person schedules, and a short screen session keeps continuity. Examination fortnights: a focused thirty-minute call to fix one technique issue is worth more than a cancelled ninety-minute visit. And travel disruption on either side, which in this city needs no explanation. Most families here end up on a hybrid pattern by the second term without planning it.

The trade-offs are real in both directions and we will not sell you one format as strictly better. Online needs a device, a usable connection and a room with a door that closes; a shared bedroom at homework hour defeats it. It makes disengagement harder for a tutor to spot in a younger child. In-person tuition costs more because travel is unpaid work for the tutor unless it is priced in, is fragile in bad weather, and commits you to a fixed hour in a city where hours move. An IB private tutor Worli families stay with for two years is usually one who switches format for a week when it makes sense, rather than defending a format on principle.

sections.heading: No lock-in: what happens when an IB Gram match in Mumbai goes wrong
paragraphs: Some matches do not work, and a platform that cannot say so is not worth using. The failure modes are predictable. The commonest is misdiagnosis: the tutor has been reteaching content when the loss was in technique, or drilling past papers when the underlying concept was never secure. Second is pace, where a careful tutor is too slow for a quick student or a brisk one leaves a slower child behind. Third is personality, which is nobody's fault and is usually visible within three sessions. Fourth, and rarest among checked tutors, is reliability, which shows up as a second late arrival rather than a cancellation, and which ends more home tuition arrangements in Mumbai than poor teaching does.

What to do is the same in every case: write to us and be specific about what has not changed. Not a rating, a description. We ask the tutor for their written review of the same period, and compare the two. In a good share of cases, particularly the misdiagnosis one, the fix is a changed focus with the same person and takes a fortnight to show. In the rest we re-shortlist from your original brief, at no cost, with no notice period and nothing to serve out. You do not need a reason that would satisfy a committee; not working is reason enough.

Three things we will not do, so that the boundary is clear. We will not defend a tutor who is not delivering, because the match is our output and a bad one is our problem. We will not sell you additional hours as the answer to a diagnosis problem. And we will not promise an outcome to keep a booking: there are no guarantees about grades here, and anyone in Mumbai who offers one should be asked by what mechanism they intend to control an examiner's judgement. The thing we do commit to is that a replacement is free and quick, and that the second shortlist is drawn from the same verified pool with your feedback folded into the filter. sections.heading: What home classes in Mumbai can and cannot do for a grade
paragraphs: A tutor can change technique, coverage and working habits. A tutor cannot change the fact that assessment is external and moderated, that a student has to do the work between sessions, or that two years of accumulated gaps take more than a term to close. Being clear about that at the start is what makes the four-week review useful rather than defensive. At four weeks the honest markers are small: your child can say what they are working on and what they have been told to stop doing, their written work shows evidence of a method rather than a guess, and you have a short written note from the tutor you can file.

At one term, expect movement where technique drives marks. Structure in extended answers. Method marks retained in multi-step calculations. Command words answered as instructed rather than as understood. Units, state symbols, graph axes, the unglamorous mark-scheme furniture that costs students more than conceptual misunderstanding does. Conceptual repair is slower and sometimes only becomes visible in the term after. At one full examination cycle the outcome worth paying for is a student who revises in a way that works without the tutor present, because that is the part that survives the booking ending.

The limits stated plainly: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, no tutor listed here is permitted to promise one, and we are an independent tutoring platform with no affiliation to Ryan Global School, Aditya Birla World Academy, JBCN International School, Parel or any other school named on this page. We will also tell you when tutoring is not the answer. A student who is not doing any work between sessions needs a different conversation first, and a child in an early year who is struggling to read may need an assessment rather than a subject tutor. Saying that costs us a booking and saves a family a term. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai wide is not on offer here, and the reason is the same honesty: that person does not exist.

faqs.question: How do IB tuition fees work, and do you add a commission on top?
faqs.answer: The tutor states their rate to you on the discovery call, and that is the figure you work with. It varies with board and level, because Higher Level Diploma Programme work demands more preparation than middle-school work; with subject scarcity, since a Physics HL or Economics HL specialist is harder to find in South Mumbai; with session length and weekly frequency; with travel, which is why a Worli address prices differently from Thane; and with the tutor's experience of the specific components your child sits. There is no joining fee and no minimum commitment, and we do not publish a rate card because any single number would mislead most readers.

faqs.question: What if we want to stop after two sessions?
faqs.answer: You stop. There is no lock-in, no notice period and no minimum number of sessions to work through, so you pay for what has happened and nothing more. We would ask you for two lines about why, because that feedback is what makes the next shortlist better, but you are not required to justify the decision. If the issue is the tutor rather than the idea of tuition, say so and we re-shortlist from your original brief at no cost. If the issue is timing, tell us when to look again and we will leave it there.

faqs.question: How quickly can home classes start after I send the brief?
faqs.answer: For a mainstream subject at a common level, expect a shortlist within a couple of days and a first session within the week, assuming the discovery calls happen promptly. Scarce combinations take longer: a Higher Level arts subject, a less common Language B, or a narrow slot such as 6pm on Friday can take a week or more to fill properly, and we would rather take that week than send you someone who does not fit. In October, when demand peaks across Mumbai, add a few days to any estimate and expect fewer slot choices than in July.

faqs.question: Which schools near Worli do your students attend, and are you connected to them?
faqs.answer: We have no connection to any school. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any institution named here. Students we match in this part of Mumbai attend Ryan Global School, which has a Worli campus, Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo and JBCN International School, Parel, with Bombay International School at Babulnath and B.D. Somani International School at Cuffe Parade also within reach. Schools are named only so a tutor can schedule around real term dates and internal deadlines. Any tutor claiming influence with a school is overstating it and you should discount it entirely.

faqs.question: Do you arrange tutoring for the Extended Essay and Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a boundary we state before the booking. Legitimate support covers helping the student settle on a workable research question, building a timeline against the school's milestone dates, discussing method and sources, giving feedback on a draft the student has written, and teaching referencing conventions. It does not cover supplying text, generating or adjusting data, writing analysis or rewriting paragraphs in the tutor's voice. The student signs an authenticity declaration and carries the consequence, so this is not a grey area for us. Ask any tutor to describe their line out loud before the first session.

faqs.question: Can one tutor handle two subjects for the same child?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only within a continuous subject spine. A physics specialist can usually cover IGCSE physics and Diploma Programme physics for siblings or across years, and a mathematics tutor can often handle both tiers of IGCSE mathematics. Across unrelated subjects the answer is almost always no, because the assessment detail that makes a specialist worth hiring does not transfer. Two subjects normally means two tutors on two evenings, or one in person and one online for the scarcer one. In Worli that is practical, since the pool here is deep enough to fill both without compromising on either.

faqs.question: What does the written review every two to four weeks actually contain?
faqs.answer: A short note in plain language, not a scorecard. It names what was worked on, what has measurably moved, what has not moved and why the tutor thinks so, and what they intend to do next. It should reference specific work rather than attitude: a paper, a question type, a draft. If it reads as general praise, push back and ask for specifics, because a vague review is the earliest warning sign that a tutor is not tracking anything. Keep the notes. Comparing week four with week sixteen is the most reliable progress measure a parent has.

Two or three verified profiles come back, each with a free discovery call so you can ask the tutor directly about components, method and rate. Nothing is scheduled until you approve one. Written reviews follow every two to four weeks, replacements cost nothing, and there is no lock-in at any stage.

This page sets out what that actually involves: session length, what you set up at home, between-session work, how progress is reported, and what happens when a session is missed.

sections.heading: What happens between your enquiry and the first home tuition lesson in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Four things happen, in this order. You send the board, the subject and the stage your child is in, plus the locality your building sits in. IB Gram shortlists tutors who already teach that exact syllabus and can physically reach you at the hour you want. You speak to one of them about the current unit and the next deadline. Then a first session is fixed at your home, on a day and at a time you set rather than one you are offered.

The shortlist is built from the syllabus, not the subject label. A parent in Dadar asking for help with Maths is asked which Maths: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Core or at Extended, Additional Mathematics 0606 sitting on top of it, or Diploma Programme (DP) Mathematics Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level (HL). Those are four different teaching jobs and largely four different shortlists. The same fork runs through Physics, Economics and English, where the board, the tier and the paper in front of the student decide who is genuinely useful at your dining table.

Your address is weighted as heavily as the subject. A tutor living in Powai can hold a six o'clock slot in Chandivali for a full term and will struggle to hold the same slot in Nerul, because the Eastern Express Highway and the Sion-Panvel Highway do not forgive a half past five departure. So IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai is matched along a corridor wherever possible: Khar West to Santacruz West along the Western Line, Mulund West to Bhandup along the Central Line, Vashi to Seawoods along Palm Beach Road.

The phone conversation before session one is where a mismatch is cheapest to catch. Ask the tutor what the current unit is assessed by, what they would set as the first piece of written work, and how they would plan the next six weeks. If the answers are generic, say so on that call rather than three weeks later. Matching is done per subject, so a DP1 student who needs Chemistry and Mathematics usually ends up with two tutors on two evenings rather than one generalist on one.
bullets: 1. Send the board, the subject, the stage and your building's locality.
2. IB Gram shortlists tutors who teach that syllabus and can reach that address.
3. Speak to the shortlisted tutor about the current unit and the next deadline.
4. Fix a weekly day and hour that survives the Mumbai evening commute.
5. First session happens at your flat; written notes follow the same evening.

sections.heading: PYP to DP2 and Year 7 to IGCSE: which stage is your child actually in?
paragraphs: International schools here run four stages, and each one needs a different kind of session. The Primary Years Programme (PYP) covers roughly Years 1 to 5, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) Years 6 to 10, Cambridge IGCSE the two years leading to the board papers, and the Diploma Programme (DP) the final two. A parent who books an IB home tutor in Mumbai without naming the stage usually gets a competent person planning the wrong thing.

At PYP and MYP 1 to 3 the work is habit and fluency: reading stamina, number facts, writing a paragraph that answers the question actually asked. Sessions are shorter, a parent is normally within earshot, and the output worth paying for is a child who starts written work without being asked twice. There is no external exam here, which is exactly why families under-rate the stage and then buy it back at speed in Year 9.

From MYP 4 the criteria start to bite. MYP assessment is criterion-referenced, with criteria A to D in every subject, so an answer that is factually fine but ignores the criterion wording still scores badly, and a tutor spends real time on command terms. IGCSE then adds tiering. The Core and Extended decision taken in Year 10 sets a ceiling on the grade available, and it should be taken from mock performance rather than from ambition, because moving down a tier in February is far more disruptive than starting at the right one in June.

DP1 and DP2 are a different job again: six subjects with three at HL, plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Creativity, Activity, Service requirement. A DP2 tutor plans backwards from fixed dates, which are the Internal Assessment (IA) final deadline, the school mock and the May examination session. A DP1 tutor plans forwards and quietly protects the IA, because a DP1 who pushes the IA into DP2 has given away the one component they fully control.
bullets: PYP: fluency, number facts and work habits, in shorter sessions
MYP 1 to 3: subject vocabulary, command terms, written structure
MYP 4 and 5: criteria A to D, the personal project, eAssessment where a school runs it
IGCSE: the Core or Extended decision, past papers, mark scheme discipline
DP1 and DP2: HL and SL load plus IA, EE and TOK deadlines

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: what a home tutor plans around
paragraphs: Subject choice across both boards is the single decision that most changes how much tuition a family ends up buying. At IGCSE the live questions are tiering and combination: Mathematics 0580 at Core or Extended, Combined Science 0653 against separate Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, and First Language English 0500 against English as a Second Language 0510. A student on Combined Science who later wants HL Chemistry has a gap that a tutor can close, but only if someone names it in Year 11 rather than in DP1.

In the DP the equivalent fork is Higher Level against Standard Level, and Mathematics Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation. HL Physics and HL Chemistry carry more content and a harder Paper 2; AA HL carries proof and calculus that AI HL does not. A student who picked three HL sciences because a university page listed them often needs support by October of DP1, and that is a timetable problem before it is an academic one, because three HL subjects rarely fit into two free evenings.

Every one of those choices carries its own internal assessment, and that is where most of the tutoring hours go. The DP sciences want a research question narrow enough to measure in a school lab with uncertainty handled honestly. DP Mathematics wants an exploration with real mathematics in it rather than a survey with a bar chart. History wants a source-based investigation with genuine evaluation. IGCSE adds coursework or a practical paper in several subjects and an endorsed speaking component in languages, each with its own window.

Nobody teaches all IB and IGCSE subjects equally well and a tutor in Mumbai who claims to is describing availability rather than expertise. IB Gram lists tutors across all IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes around Mumbai, but the match is made one subject at a time. Asking for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai usually produces one generalist where two specialists were wanted: take a DP1 student in Bandra West carrying HL Biology, HL English, HL History, SL Mathematics AI, SL Economics and Hindi B, whose Biology IA and History investigation need the same skill and land in the same fortnight.

Combined Science 0653 against separate 0610, 0620 and 0625 papers
Maths AA against AI, and what each demands at HL

sections.heading: Where IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai actually reaches
paragraphs: Tutors are matched across all six parts of the city: South Mumbai, the Western Suburbs, the Central Suburbs, the Eastern Suburbs, Navi Mumbai and Thane. Coverage is not uniform and the honest version is that your postcode changes which hours are available to you far more than it changes which subjects are. Parents who type IB tutors near me in Mumbai into a search box are really asking about slot availability, and the answer is a travel answer.

South Mumbai covers Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Napean Sea Road, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road, Worli and Prabhadevi. Distances are short and the clock is slow: eight kilometres from Worli to Colaba can still cost forty minutes at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals, so tutors are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, with the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 slowly changing that. The Western Suburbs run north to south through Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz West, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon East, Malad West, Kandivali East and Borivali, strung along the Western Line, Metro Lines 2A and 7, the Western Express Highway and Link Road. Matching along that spine works; matching across it at seven in the evening does not.

The Central Suburbs take in Powai, Chandivali, Ghatkopar East, Vikhroli, Kanjurmarg and Mulund West, held together by the Central Line, Metro Line 1, the Eastern Express Highway and JVLR. Powai is the exception worth knowing: it is physically central but has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and a JVLR jam turns a twenty minute trip into an hour. The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund East on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway makes South Mumbai reachable from Chembur and Wadala much faster than the map suggests.

Navi Mumbai is built in nodes, so Vashi, Sanpada, Nerul, Seawoods, CBD Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 filling in. Tutors are matched node to node; pulling one across the creek for a weekday evening, even over the Atal Setu, rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads from the station out along Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Ghodbunder Road and Kasarvadavali, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the timetable, since a tutor near the station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at eight.
bullets: South Mumbai: matched within the island, not brought down from Andheri
Western Suburbs: match along the Western Line, not across the highway

Eastern Suburbs: the Eastern Freeway makes Chembur to Fort unexpectedly quick

sections.heading: How the IB and IGCSE assessment calendar lands on a Mumbai school year
paragraphs: The school year here opens in June, and the assessment calendar is what a tutor plans a term around. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Oberoi International School in Goregaon East, Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul are working to the same external dates even though their internal schedules differ. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page, nor with the International Baccalaureate organisation or Cambridge International Education; naming a school here only tells you whose calendar a tutor will be working around.

The first pressure point arrives sooner than parents expect. Between late September and the Diwali break, DP1 students are usually expected to produce an EE research question and a first supervisor meeting, DP2 students have science and mathematics IA drafts in motion, and IGCSE Year 11 cohorts sit a first round of internal tests that schools use to confirm Core or Extended entries. A tutor who starts in August has time to shape that work. A tutor who starts in late October is triaging it.

January and February are the hardest weeks in the year. Mock examinations, IA final deadlines and the TOK essay arrive within about a fortnight of each other for most DP2 cohorts, and Year 11 mocks decide predicted grades that are already sitting in university applications. A DP2 student in Chembur can have a Physics IA final, a TOK essay upload and a Mathematics mock inside the same week, which is a sequencing problem, not a content problem, and a good home tutor spends those sessions deciding what gets dropped rather than adding anything.

After that the calendar empties out fast. The Cambridge IGCSE May and June series and the DP May session sit on the far side of study leave in April, so March sessions move to full timed papers under exam conditions and April sessions become short, frequent and targeted at specific papers. Families whose school enters students for the October and November IGCSE series run the same cycle six months out of step, which is worth saying on the first call, because an out of phase calendar changes which tutors are free.
bullets: June to September: build the base while nothing is due
Late September to Diwali: EE question, IA drafts, tier-confirming tests
January and February: mocks, IA finals and the TOK essay collide
March: full timed papers at home under exam conditions
April and May: short targeted sessions through study leave and the exam series

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or a mix of both: what each is like in Mumbai
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default for a reason: the tutor sits beside the student, sees the working as it is written, catches the wrong first step before the page is full, and leaves the parent able to hear whether the hour was spent on anything. IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai is one to one at your table, with the tutor carrying the syllabus, the past papers and the mark schemes. The cost of that is rigidity. A tutor crossing Mumbai in the evening can hold one slot well and two badly, so the day and hour become close to fixed for the term.

Online removes the travel and buys back choice. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can teach a Cuffe Parade student from Thane, which matters when the subject is scarce, and scarcity is real for HL Further Mathematics, Music, Psychology, Latin and some Group 2 languages. It also survives a monsoon evening when a tutor physically cannot reach Kasarvadavali or Panvel. What you give up is supervision: a Year 8 student alone with a laptop drifts, and a student who hides a blank page on camera can hide it for several weeks. Online needs a tablet with a stylus or a document camera so the tutor sees pen on paper, not a finished photograph.

Hybrid is what most families actually settle into by the second term, and it is worth planning deliberately rather than falling into. The pattern that holds is a weekly session at home for the teaching, plus a short online slot in the two days before a deadline for a draft read or a mark scheme check. It costs less travel, keeps the face to face hour intact, and gives you a way to add help in January without finding a new evening in an already full week.

An IB private tutor Mumbai families book for a single scarce subject is often the clearest case for going online from the start, while a child who needs the structure of someone arriving at the door is the clearest case against it. Decide on the student, not on the convenience. The wrong call here shows up as a tutor who is always slightly late or a student who is always slightly absent, and both are fixable in week two rather than month three.
bullets: Home: the tutor sees working as it happens; the slot becomes fixed
Online: wider choice of specialists, survives monsoon evenings, weaker supervision
Online needs a stylus tablet or document camera, not a phone camera
Hybrid: weekly session at home plus a short pre-deadline online check
Younger students and drifters do better with someone at the door

sections.heading: Who is standing at your door, and how was that tutor checked?
paragraphs: Before a tutor is listed, IB Gram checks government photo identity, the academic and teaching record behind the subject being claimed, and which board and which syllabus that person has actually taught rather than merely studied. A subject conversation follows, because somebody who has taught IGCSE Chemistry 0620 can say without pausing which paper the practical skills are assessed on and what a mark scheme rewards in a six mark explanation. References are taken where a tutor has them. Anyone matched for IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai has been through that before your enquiry reaches them.

Then there is the part only you can do, at the door and in the first fortnight. Check the photo identity against the person standing there on the first visit, and register the tutor at your society gate as a recurring visitor rather than a one-off, so a weekly entry does not become a weekly argument. Most larger complexes in Powai, Kharghar, Thane West and Goregaon East now run app-based gate passes, and a standing weekly pass takes one message to the committee or the facility manager.

In the first few sessions, keep the lesson in a shared room with the door open and within normal earshot. This is not suspicion, it is how you find out whether the hour is being taught or filled. You should be able to hear questions being asked of your child rather than a continuous monologue, and you should see written work leaving the table. If a tutor prefers a closed door, that is a reasonable thing to decline.

Ask three questions in week one and you will know what you have. Which paper and which component is the current unit assessed by? What did you set, and when will you mark it? What are we doing in six weeks that we are not doing now? A tutor who cannot answer the first is in the wrong subject, one who cannot answer the second is not setting work, and one who cannot answer the third has no plan beyond the next hour.
bullets: Checked before listing: photo identity, subject record, boards actually taught
A subject conversation about papers, components and mark schemes
Your job: match the identity at the door on visit one
Register a standing weekly gate pass, not a visitor pass each week
Keep early sessions in a shared room with the door open

sections.heading: What a home tuition session actually consists of, from session one to session five
paragraphs: Session one is a diagnosis and it should feel slightly underwhelming. The tutor reads the school's current unit plan, looks at the last two marked assessments, asks the student to attempt one question cold, and sets a single piece of written work before leaving. Very little new content is taught. By session five the shape has settled: roughly ten minutes reviewing the set work, thirty-five teaching the current unit against the mark scheme, fifteen on a past paper question written under time, and five setting the next task and writing it down where the parent can see it.

Session length and frequency follow the stage, not the budget. Sixty minutes is right for PYP and MYP 1 to 3, because attention goes before the hour does. Ninety minutes is right for IGCSE and DP, since a full Paper 4 question set, a marked review and a taught concept do not fit into sixty. Twice a week is worth it in the term before the papers or when a subject is genuinely behind; once a week plus a short pre-deadline check is enough the rest of the year. Two signs you chose wrong: the child visibly fades around the seventieth minute, or set work is still unfinished when the tutor arrives.

What each side brings matters more than the room does. The tutor brings the current syllabus, a question bank, past papers and mark schemes, and notes from last week, not a textbook of their own invention. You provide a hard table at the right height, a chair the student can sit up in, light that is not behind them, a plug point, and a television that is off. The student has ready before the doorbell: the school notebook, the last marked test with the teacher's comments still on it, the current assignment brief with its due date, the school textbook, and the calculator model the school allows, which for DP Mathematics usually means an approved graphic display calculator.

Good between-session work is one markable task, not a stack of worksheets. Three past paper questions with the mark scheme withheld, a redraft of one IA paragraph against a single criterion, a set of command term cards, a corrected version of the last test with reasons written beside each correction: each of these is finishable in a sitting and reviewable in ten minutes. The test of whether it is working is simple. If the set work is never looked at again at the start of the next session, you are paying for a lecture rather than teaching, and that is worth raising immediately.
bullets: Session one: read the unit plan, review marked work, set one task
Session five: review, teach against the mark scheme, timed question, set work
60 minutes for PYP and lower MYP; 90 minutes for IGCSE and DP
Twice weekly in the exam term; weekly plus a deadline check otherwise
Set work must be markable, dated and reviewed at the next session
A missed session is rescheduled, not dropped, inside the same week where possible

sections.heading: How do you know it is working after four weeks in Mumbai?
paragraphs: At four weeks, do not look at grades. What should have changed is that your child can say what a question is asking and can start it without being rescued, that set work comes back finished, and that the tutor's notes name specific weaknesses rather than describing the lesson. At one term, expect mark scheme literate answers, one internal assessment or class test moving, and fewer blank starts. At one full exam cycle, the evidence is the school's own predicted grade conversation, which is the only measure you did not pay for.

Progress is reported in three layers, and all three should exist. Written notes arrive after each session, saying what was covered, what was set and what was weak. A short summary each month states what moved and what did not, which is where an honest tutor says a topic is still failing. The school report and the teacher meeting are the external check, and if those three disagree, the school is right and the question becomes why the sessions are not reaching what the school is marking.

The limits are worth stating plainly. A tutor cannot fix poor school attendance, cannot write an IA or an EE and should refuse to, cannot change moderation applied to a whole cohort, and cannot compress two years of missed foundations into the eight weeks before a May session. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no tutor here will promise one. Parents sometimes ask who the best IB tutor in Mumbai is; the honest answer is that the question has no city-wide answer, because the right tutor is defined by one board, one subject, one tier and one free evening.

If the match is wrong, say so after the second session rather than the eighth. The usual signals are a tutor who re-teaches the school lesson instead of the gap, who never sets work, or who simply does not get on with your child, and none of those improve with time. A replacement starts from where you are: the session notes are handed over, the weekly slot is kept where the new tutor's travel allows, and the first session picks up from the last marked work rather than beginning the diagnosis again. Changing once is normal; changing three times usually means the subject or the stage was described imprecisely at the start.
bullets: Four weeks: work gets started and finished, notes name specific gaps
One term: mark scheme literate answers and one assessment moving
One exam cycle: the school's predicted grade conversation is the real check
Reported in three layers: session notes, monthly summary, school report
Raise a bad match after session two; a replacement keeps the slot and the notes

sections.heading: Setting up your first home tuition session anywhere in Mumbai
paragraphs: Four documents make the first session useful instead of exploratory: the most recent school report, the last two marked assessments with teacher comments intact, the school's assessment calendar for the term, and the subject guide or syllabus the school is following. Photograph them and send them with the enquiry. A tutor who has read a marked paper before arriving spends session one teaching rather than discovering, and that is the cheapest hour you will ever save.

Decide three things before you call. Which subject genuinely comes first, because starting two at once in January rarely works. Which two evenings are actually free once school transport, sport and the commute home are counted. And who will be in the flat during the session, since that answer shapes whether home or hybrid is the right call for a younger student. Families in Mira Road, Vashi and Mulund West who book a six o'clock slot without checking the school bus arrival time usually end up moving it within a fortnight.

On fees, the useful thing to know is what moves the number rather than what the number is. IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board and the level, with HL and Extended work costing more than SL and Core, on how scarce the subject is, on how far the tutor travels and at what hour, on session length, on whether the sessions are one to one or shared between siblings, and on whether you are booking through the year or in the weeks before a paper. Scarcity and travel are the two that surprise people most.

The first session itself covers the diagnosis, the plan and the first task, and ends with a date. Within two days you should have the session notes and a six week outline naming the units and the deadlines it is built around. If either is missing, ask once; if it is still missing, that is your week two signal rather than your month two regret. Everything after that is routine: same evening, same table, work set and work marked.
bullets: Send the report, two marked papers, the term calendar and the syllabus
Pick one subject to start, not three
Confirm two evenings that survive school transport and the commute
Fees move on board, level, subject scarcity, travel, hour and session length

faqs.question: What does IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai actually include?
faqs.answer: One checked subject specialist, teaching your child one to one at your home on a fixed weekly slot, working from the school's own syllabus and deadlines. Practically that means a diagnostic first session built on your child's marked work, a six week plan tied to the assessment calendar, one markable task set between sessions, written notes after every lesson, and a monthly summary of what moved. IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai is matched per subject, so two subjects usually mean two tutors on two evenings. Materials are the tutor's responsibility: syllabus, past papers and mark schemes, not a book you buy.

faqs.question: How long should each home tuition session be, and how often?
faqs.answer: Sixty minutes for PYP and MYP 1 to 3, ninety for IGCSE and DP. The reason is mechanical rather than commercial: a full Paper 4 question set, a review of marked work and one taught concept do not fit into an hour, while a Year 4 student stops absorbing well before sixty minutes are up. Weekly is enough for most of the year, with a short check before a deadline. Twice weekly earns its place in the term before the papers, or when a subject is genuinely behind. If your child fades around the seventieth minute, shorten the session instead of pushing through it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to my building on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the hour you pick decides how reliably. Four to six in the evening is the easiest window to fill anywhere in the city. Seven to nine is contested, and travel is what breaks it: a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali on Ghodbunder Road in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at eight, and crossing Peddar Road southbound at seven costs the same. This is why matching is done along a corridor rather than across the city. If only a late slot works for your family, expect a shorter shortlist and consider a hybrid arrangement for one of the two sessions.

faqs.question: What do I need to set up at home before the first session?
faqs.answer: A hard table at the right height, a chair your child can sit upright in, light that is not behind them, a plug point within reach and a television that is off. Keep it in a shared room rather than a bedroom, at least for the first few weeks. Your child should have ready before the doorbell: the school notebook, the last marked test with comments on it, the current assignment brief and its due date, the school textbook, and the calculator model the school permits. Nothing else is needed. The tutor brings the syllabus, the question bank, past papers and mark schemes.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed, or the tutor is stuck commuting?
faqs.answer: It is rescheduled inside the same week wherever possible, not written off. The practical convention is simple: a cancellation with reasonable notice on either side moves the slot, and a tutor who is delayed by rain or a jam on JVLR tells you before the start time rather than after it. Mumbai makes this routine in the monsoon, which is one reason a hybrid arrangement is useful, since a session that cannot happen in Panvel or Kasarvadavali in person can often still happen online that evening. Two or three missed sessions in a term with no reschedule offered is a matching problem, and worth raising.

faqs.question: How is between-session work set and checked?
faqs.answer: One markable task per session, written down where you can see it, reviewed at the start of the next lesson. Good examples: three past paper questions with the mark scheme withheld until afterwards, a redraft of one IA paragraph against a single criterion, or a corrected version of the last class test with a reason written beside each correction. Each is finishable in one sitting and reviewable in ten minutes. The check is whether it is ever looked at again. If set work is never reviewed, the sessions have become lectures, and that is a conversation to have in week two.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work as well as a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: For a motivated IGCSE or DP student, close to it; for a younger or drifting student, no. An IB online tutor in Mumbai can teach a Cuffe Parade student from Thane, which matters when the subject is scarce, as it is for HL Further Mathematics, Psychology, Music and some languages. It also saves a monsoon evening. What it costs you is supervision and visible working, so online needs a stylus tablet or a document camera rather than a phone photograph of a finished page. Most families end up hybrid: the teaching hour at home, a short online check before deadlines.

faqs.question: There is no visible progress after a month. What now?
faqs.answer: At four weeks, grades are the wrong measure, so first check the right ones: is work being started without rescue, is set work coming back finished, and do the session notes name specific weaknesses rather than describing the lesson? If those three are happening, keep going; content takes a term to show in marks. If any is missing, ask the tutor for the six week plan in writing and compare it against what the school is actually marking. A plan that does not match the school's calendar is the usual cause, and it is fixable without changing tutors.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, then scarcity, travel and time. HL and Extended work costs more than SL and Core because the content and the marking load are heavier. A scarce subject costs more than a common one at the same level. IB tuition fees in Mumbai also move with how far a tutor travels and at what hour, with session length, with whether sessions are one to one or shared between siblings, and with whether you book across the year or in the weeks before a paper. IB Gram does not publish a single rate card, because a ninety minute HL Physics session in Panvel and a sixty minute MYP session in Khar West are not the same job.

faqs.question: How do I change tutors if the match is wrong?
faqs.answer: Say so after the second session and ask for a replacement; you do not have to justify it academically. The session notes are handed to the new tutor, the weekly slot is kept where their travel allows, and the first session resumes from the last marked work instead of repeating the whole diagnosis. Common reasons are a tutor who re-teaches the school lesson rather than the gap, one who never sets work, and a personality mismatch, and none of the three improves with patience. Changing once is normal. Changing three times usually means the subject, the tier or the stage was described loosely at the start.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with my child's school or with the IB?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school, to the International Baccalaureate organisation or to Cambridge International Education. Schools are named on this page only as local context, because their calendars set the deadlines a tutor plans around and their board pathways decide which syllabus is being taught. Nobody here speaks for a school, sees its internal marking, or can influence a predicted grade. What a tutor can do is prepare your child for what that school is assessing, on the dates the school has published, which is the part that is actually within anyone's control.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor cover all of my child's subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually not well, and it is worth resisting. A single tutor can reasonably hold two related subjects at the same stage, such as Physics and Mathematics at IGCSE, or Economics and Business Management at SL. Across three HL subjects in different groups, depth goes first and you end up paying for supervision rather than teaching. The practical pattern is one specialist per demanding subject and one evening each, with the lighter subjects handled by the school plus set work. If evenings are the constraint, pick the subject with the nearest assessment and start there.

ibgram-home-tuition.closingCta: Send the subject, the stage and your locality, with photographs of the last two marked papers and the term's assessment calendar. You will get a shortlist of tutors who teach that syllabus and can reach your building at the hour you asked for, a call with the one you pick, and a first session at your table. Within two days of it, expect written notes and a six week plan naming the deadlines it is built around.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram pick a home tutor for your child in Mumbai?
paragraphs: By narrowing in a fixed order: first the board and syllabus version your child actually sits, then the subject at the level they take it, then the travel window that works from your address on a weekday evening, and only then teaching style. An IB Gram home tutor in Mumbai is never matched on a subject label alone, because Physics at Higher Level and Physics at Standard Level are different jobs taught from different paper structures.

The request a parent sends is usually short: Maths, Grade 10, Khar West, evenings. The useful version is longer, and the first call exists to get it. Which board, and which first examination year. Which paper the last test came from. What the school report said in words rather than in a grade. Whether the child sat silent through the last tutor or argued with them. Whether anyone is at home between seven and nine. Each answer removes tutors from the shortlist, and removing tutors is the entire point of the exercise.

Shortlists are kept deliberately small. Two or three names a family can actually read beats a list they will skim. Each name arrives with the board history that matters: which syllabus versions the tutor has taught, which internal assessments they have supervised and had moderated, how long they have taught that subject at that level, and the zones they can reach for a standing weekly slot. Travel is treated as a hard constraint rather than a preference, because a tutor who can reach you in April cannot necessarily reach you in July once the rain starts.

Then it stops being our judgement and becomes yours. The trial session is where a shortlist becomes a decision, and the questions further down this page are the ones worth asking in it. If the fit is wrong, say so early. A replacement is a normal event rather than a complaint, and the second match is usually better because the first one told us something the enquiry form did not.
bullets: 1. Send the board, subject, level, school and your address.
2. A short call fixes syllabus version, recent papers and timing.
3. Two or three tutor profiles reach you with board history attached.
4. You run a trial session and watch how your child responds.
5. Confirm a weekly slot, or ask for a different tutor.

sections.heading: Why board experience beats general brilliance in IB DP and IGCSE
paragraphs: The International Baccalaureate (IB) and Cambridge International Education do not reward the same answer. A Diploma Programme (DP) Biology paper question that says evaluate expects a judgement supported on both sides; a question that says outline expects a short list and gives no credit for the essay a bright student wants to write instead. A tutor who has never read the subject guide's command term list will coach good science and still lose marks. That is why board history, not degree prestige, is the first filter on any profile.

Each programme carries its own internal machinery. Middle Years Programme (MYP) subjects are marked against four criteria with published strands, so an MYP Year 5 student is not chasing a percentage but evidence against criterion C or criterion D. The DP adds an Internal Assessment (IA) in every subject, plus the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), each with its own criteria and its own failure modes. International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) subjects split into Core and Extended tiers, where Core caps the grade available and Extended assumes material the Core syllabus never teaches.

Those structures decide who can actually help. A tutor with years of Higher Level (HL) Mathematics Analysis and Approaches has internalised which topics the investigative paper tends to reach into; a tutor fresh from an engineering degree has not. An IGCSE Extended Additional Mathematics student and a Core Mathematics student need different tutors, not different amounts of the same tutor. When a family asks for an IB home tutor in Mumbai without naming the level, the level is the first thing we go back and ask about.

Level decisions are part of the tutoring work rather than a separate conversation with the school. A DP1 student carrying three HLs they chose in a hurry has a scheduling problem before they have a subject problem, and a tutor who has taught both HL and Standard Level (SL) can tell you honestly whether dropping one is a retreat or a correction. Searches like all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes Mumbai land on this page for that reason: the structure question comes before the tutor question.
bullets: Command terms differ by board; marks follow the verb, not effort.
MYP marks against criteria and strands, not against percentages.
IGCSE Core caps the top grade; Extended assumes extra content.
Every DP subject carries an Internal Assessment with its own criteria.
HL and SL share topics but not depth or paper structure.

sections.heading: Does your tutor know the subject, or can they actually teach it?
paragraphs: Those are two separate abilities and the second one is rarer. Knowing Chemistry means getting the right answer. Teaching Chemistry means knowing the four wrong routes a Grade 11 student takes towards that answer, recognising from half a sentence which one this child is on, and asking the question that exposes it rather than supplying the correct method and moving on.

You can hear the difference inside a trial session. A tutor who only knows the subject explains, and explains well, and the child nods. A tutor who can teach it stops talking. They set part of a question, watch the pen, and interrupt at the step where it went wrong instead of at the end. They ask what made you choose that formula. They leave a silence long enough to be uncomfortable. In a DP Economics session they will make the student label the diagram's axes before drawing anything, because that is exactly where the marks leak away.

Subject depth across both boards means the specific components, not the subject name. For English, that is the DP Individual Oral with its global issue and its two extracts, and the IGCSE First Language directed writing task. For Mathematics, the graphic display calculator conventions that earn method marks. For the sciences, an IA with a defensible independent variable rather than an interesting idea. For Business Management, the HL extension topics and the stimulus-based case study. A tutor should be able to say which of those they have taken a student through from start to finish.

Subject choice and the HL or SL call sit on top of all of this, and they are tutoring conversations too. A student who loves Chemistry but cannot write a conclusion will struggle more in DP Chemistry HL than in SL, and a good tutor says so in the first month rather than the second term. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families imagine is rarely one person. It is the right person per subject, which is why a sibling pair often ends up with two tutors.
bullets: Ask which papers and components the tutor has taught end to end.
Watch whether the tutor diagnoses the error or restates the method.
A good tutor names the marking criterion a student keeps losing.
Subject choice and HL or SL calls belong in early sessions.
One specialist per subject beats one generalist across five.

sections.heading: Which Mumbai zones have deep tutor supply, and which are thin?
paragraphs: Supply follows the schools, so it is deepest where IB and IGCSE schools cluster. In Mumbai, Maharashtra that means South Mumbai first, where Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Fort, Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Worli sit within a short but slow drive of each other on the Western Line, the Harbour Line and the new Coastal Road. Tutors here are matched inside the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, and the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at the evening peak cost more time than the distance suggests, so a six o'clock slot in Colaba and a six o'clock slot in Worli are not interchangeable.

The Western Suburbs are the deepest pool in the city. Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri West, Goregaon, Malad, Kandivali and Borivali run north to south along the Western Express Highway, the Western Line, Link Road and Metro Lines 2A and 7, and matching along that line works far better than matching across it. The Central Suburbs follow the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway through Kurla, Ghatkopar, Vikhroli and Mulund, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the Jogeshwari Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR) in between. Powai is the odd case: physically central, no station of its own, reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, which is why its evening slots fill first.

The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines, and the Eastern Freeway and the Monorail put Chembur and Wadala closer to South Mumbai than the map implies, which matters when an island tutor takes a Chembur slot. Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel each sit a short run from the next on Palm Beach Road and the Sion Panvel Highway; tutors are matched node to node, and the Atal Setu has made a Nerul tutor viable in Wadala in a way the Trans-Harbour Line alone never did. Thane spreads from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, where Kasarvadavali is twenty minutes away off-peak and close to an hour in the evening.

Thin supply is not the same as no supply. For an HL Further Mathematics tutor in Kharghar, or a DP Visual Arts tutor in Mulund, the honest answer is often a hybrid: home tuition fortnightly with the specialist and online contact in the weeks between. That is a scheduling fact about this city rather than a judgement about your address, and saying it up front is better than booking a weekly slot nobody can hold.
bullets: South Mumbai: short distances, slow signals, island-matched tutors.
Western Suburbs: deepest supply; match along the line, not across it.
Powai has no station; road access from Andheri East or Ghatkopar.
Navi Mumbai matches node to node; Atal Setu widened the options.
Thane schedules revolve around Ghodbunder Road at the evening peak.
Scarce subjects at any address usually mean a hybrid timetable.

sections.heading: What your child's school calendar says about the tutor you need
paragraphs: School names matter here as calendar information and nothing more. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in Bandra Kurla Complex, at Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, at Oberoi International School on JVLR, at Bombay International School near Babulnath and the Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, at Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, at Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and at D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all work to an assessment rhythm their own school sets. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of those schools or with any examination board.

That rhythm decides which tutor you want and when you want them. A May-session DP school pushes most Internal Assessment drafts into the second half of DP1 and the opening weeks of DP2, which means September to November is when a tutor's IA supervision experience matters more than their exam drilling. Mock examinations land in the winter months, and the useful tutor in January is the one who can read a mock script and separate a knowledge gap from a timing problem. IGCSE candidates sitting the May and June series meet coursework deadlines months before that.

The monsoon is the other calendar, and it is the one families forget when they book. June and July break more tutoring schedules in Mumbai than examinations do, and the tutor who holds a slot through a flooded Andheri subway or a stalled Western Line is the one who agreed in advance to move that session online rather than cancel it. Ask a prospective tutor what they did last July. The answer tells you more about reliability than any certificate does, and reliability across a term is worth more than one brilliant session in September.

School-specific claims are where you should be most careful. A tutor who says they know how a particular school marks, or that they have seen its internal grade boundaries, is either repeating a staffroom rumour or describing access they should not have. A tutor who says they have taught several students through that school's DP timeline and knows when its drafts fall is describing ordinary experience. Those two sentences sound similar in a phone call and they are not remotely the same thing.
bullets: Ask when the school's IA drafts and mock examinations actually fall.
September to November favours tutors with Internal Assessment experience.
