faqs.question: Will a tutor commute to Cumballa Hill for a Saturday morning session?
faqs.answer: Saturday mornings are often the easiest slot to fill, because the signals at Peddar Road and Haji Ali are clear and a tutor can cross South Mumbai in a fraction of the weekday time. Many families use Saturday deliberately for the longer teaching session and keep a short weekday slot for review. The one caution is consistency: Saturdays compete with family plans, matches, and school events, and a slot that gets cancelled twice a month is worse than a protected weekday evening. If you take Saturday, protect it like a weekday.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: For in-person sessions, an adult in the house is sensible but does not need to be in the room. Sitting in changes how a fifteen-year-old answers questions, and most tutors work better without an audience. What helps is being available at the end for two minutes so the tutor can tell you what happened. For online sessions the requirement is firmer: somebody should be in the house, the student should be at a desk, and the work should be visible on camera, or the session quietly stops being one.

faqs.question: Is an Extended tier tutor more expensive than a Core tier one?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, modestly, because Extended material needs a tutor who has taught the harder papers and that pool is smaller. The bigger cost driver is not the tier, though. IGCSE tuition fees in Cumballa Hill move most with how scarce the specification is locally, how far the tutor travels at peak hour, how long and frequent the sessions are, and how much marking happens between them. When you compare two quotes, make sure they assume the same session length and the same amount of marked work, or you are not comparing anything.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects should my child take?
faqs.answer: Fewer than the maximum, in most cases. Carrying nine subjects where two are collapsing produces worse outcomes than carrying seven done properly, and the weakest subject usually consumes the evenings that the strong ones needed. Schools differ in what they allow, so ask the coordinator what the minimum entry is and what dropping one would cost for later subject choices. This decision belongs in Year 9 or early Year 10. By the second term of Year 11, the realistic response to overload is triage rather than reduction.

faqs.question: Should we start tutoring in Year 9 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 9 or early Year 10, if the aim is improvement rather than rescue. Habits set in that window, the content is still thin enough to repair properly, and the tier conversation is still open. Waiting until Year 11 means paying for triage: a tutor who has to choose between covering missing content and drilling technique, and who can rarely do both well in thirty sessions. If money is the constraint, two terms of help in Year 10 buys more than four terms of help in Year 11.

faqs.question: Core or Extended: who actually decides?
faqs.answer: The school decides the entry, usually on the evidence of internal assessment, and parents can ask for it to be reviewed but cannot simply choose. What you can do is bring evidence. If your child was placed on Core after a bad term and has since been scoring well on Extended-style questions, a tutor can produce marked work at that standard for the coordinator to look at. Do this in Year 9 or the first half of Year 10, while the entry is still genuinely open rather than administratively closed.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the alternative-to-practical paper without a lab?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is one of the clearest wins in IGCSE tutoring. The paper tests whether a student can read apparatus, identify variables, criticise a method, record data sensibly and interpret a graph. All of that is trainable at a dining table with past papers and a pencil. What a tutor cannot replace is the experience of having actually done the experiments, so the honest approach is to pair practical work at school with method criticism at home rather than treating one as a substitute for the other.

faqs.question: What if my child is sitting a later series instead of the main one?
faqs.answer: Then the whole plan shifts and the tutor needs to know on day one. A later series means a different revision peak, a different relationship to the school's own teaching calendar, and often a student working partly alone on a syllabus their class has moved past. Those arrangements work, but they need more structure, not less: a written scheme of work, fixed weekly written output, and a mock sat under timed conditions at home. Confirm the entry details with the school in writing before you plan anything.

faqs.question: Does a tutor from a Cambridge background handle Pearson Edexcel papers?
faqs.answer: Often, but ask rather than assume. The content overlap between Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel specifications is large, so a strong subject teacher will recognise the material. What differs is paper structure and question wording, and a tutor who has never marked the second board's papers will spend the first month learning them on your time. Ask directly which specifications they have taught and in which years. A tutor who says they can teach any board without naming one is not the match.

faqs.question: What notice is needed to change our weekly evening slot?
faqs.answer: A week, as a rule, because an IGCSE home tutor in Cumballa Hill is holding that time against other families and the slot before it determines whether they can reach you. Occasional one-off moves are normal around school events and festivals, and most tutors will accommodate a day's notice once in a while. Repeated changes are what kill arrangements: the tutor loses the adjacent booking that made your slot viable, and the student stops treating the session as fixed. Agree the notice rule in the first week.

faqs.question: Why will no tutor put a predicted grade in writing?
faqs.answer: Because nobody can honestly do it, and the ones who try are selling rather than teaching. IB Gram does not guarantee grades. What a good tutor can put in writing is far more useful: what the diagnosis was, which topics are being covered in what order, what written work will be set, and what the student should be able to do by a stated date. Those are checkable commitments. If you want a realistic grade range, ask the subject teacher at school, who has the internal evidence and the mock scripts.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: which IGCSE is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: Ask the school which board, in writing, before you hire anybody. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both run international qualifications at this level, both are commonly called IGCSE in Mumbai, and they are not interchangeable. The subject content overlaps heavily. The question papers, the component structure, the command words and the mark schemes do not. A tutor who has spent six years on Cambridge papers will teach a Pearson Edexcel student competently, but will not know by instinct where that board's examiners award and withhold marks, and at this level instinct is most of what you are paying for.

Inside each board there is a second decision that matters more than most parents are told. Several subjects are offered at two tiers, Core and Extended in the Cambridge system, with different grade ranges available from each. The tier a child is entered for in Year 10 shapes which subjects they can realistically continue at Higher Level in the Diploma Programme two years later, and it is set by the school, not by you. A good IGCSE home tutor in Dadar Parsi Colony will tell you honestly whether an Extended entry is a stretch worth making or a decision that will cost marks across the whole paper.

There is also the question of which series your child sits. Schools around Dadar and Matunga enter candidates in different examination series, and some enter strong candidates early in one or two subjects. That changes a tutoring plan completely: a subject being sat in one series while the rest are sat in another means a tutor is running two calendars in the same house. Confirm the series per subject with the examinations coordinator, because the structure of components and their current requirements are revised by the boards on their own cycles and the only reliable source is the current syllabus document for the year your child actually sits.

Parents who search for the best IGCSE tutor in Dadar Parsi Colony are usually really asking a board question without knowing it. The honest answer is that the strongest available tutor for a Pearson Edexcel candidate is the one who has marked or taught that board's papers, not the one with the longest list of subjects. We would rather tell you we do not currently have the right board match for a scarce subject than place a tutor who will learn the paper alongside your child.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects and tiers should a Year 9 student commit to?
paragraphs: Commit to the subjects your child can argue for, not the ones that look strongest on paper. A Year 9 choice form in a Mumbai international school typically asks for a spread across languages, humanities, sciences and mathematics, with two or three genuinely free slots. Those free slots are where families get it wrong. A child who chooses three separate sciences because a cousin did medicine will spend Year 11 writing six science papers and resenting all of them. A tutor who knows the subject landscape across both boards is useful at exactly this moment, before the form is submitted.

Subject choice across both boards, HL and SL thinking, Core and Extended decisions, and the internal assessments each one carries are all part of the same conversation. Several IGCSE subjects carry coursework or a practical component that is assessed inside the school and submitted on a school deadline, not an examination-hall deadline. That matters for planning, because those deadlines land in term time and they do not move. A child taking a language, a creative subject and a science may have three school-set submission dates inside the same fortnight in Year 11, and no amount of past paper practice in April will rescue a component that was handed in thin.

Within each subject the useful work is narrower than parents expect. In Mathematics the recurring mark losses sit in bounds and accuracy, transformations, similar shapes and the scale factor applied to area and volume, and in reading a structured question as a sequence of dependent parts. In the sciences they sit in defining terms precisely and in handling data: drawing a line of best fit that respects anomalies, quoting a reading to the right precision, and explaining a trend rather than describing it. In English and the humanities they sit in answering the command word that was actually used.

This is why we match by paper rather than by subject label. A Dadar Parsi Colony tutor working with a Year 11 Chemistry candidate spends more time on structured response discipline than on new content, and a tutor working with a Year 9 student spends almost all of it on algebraic fluency so that the Year 10 content has somewhere to land. We cover all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 level with a tutor Mumbai parents can interview before any money changes hands.

South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow, and parents consistently underestimate the second half of that sentence. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. A tutor travelling the same eight kilometres from Matunga to Parsi Colony at the same hour arrives on time, because the journey never touches those signals. This is why we match within the island rather than bringing tutors down from the suburbs, and why a tutor who lives in Andheri and promises a 6.30pm slot in Dadar Parsi Colony is making a promise the road will break.

The corridor matters more than the distance on a map. None of those help a tutor coming east to west across the island in the evening. A tutor who already teaches in Matunga on a Tuesday can add a Parsi Colony student at 7pm on the same evening and the whole arrangement holds for a full term. That is the arrangement we try to build.

sections.heading: The Mumbai IGCSE calendar that decides when you should start
paragraphs: Families here send children to a spread of international schools rather than one dominant local option. Don Bosco International School and JBCN International School, Parel are both reachable from Parsi Colony, and between them they account for a good share of the IGCSE candidates in these lanes. Naming them is local context and nothing more. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel, or any other school mentioned anywhere on this page.

What those schools share is a calendar, and the calendar is what should drive your hiring decision. The academic year opens after the monsoon break with a long stretch of new content. The first real signal arrives with the term assessments, and that is when most parents in Mumbai start searching. By the time the mock series runs, the useful window for fixing a content gap in a Year 11 subject is already narrowing, and what is left is paper technique. Starting in the first term costs the same per session as starting in the last one and buys perhaps three times the benefit.

The pressure points are predictable. School-set coursework and practical components come due in term time, usually clustered, and a child taking three subjects with internal components will meet them in the same few weeks. Mocks land in the middle of the year and are the only honest data most parents get before the real thing. The final series then runs in the examination window the school has entered your child for, with study leave immediately before it. Between the mock results and study leave is the period when home tuition in Mumbai is hardest to book, because every family in the city has reached the same conclusion in the same fortnight.

There is a quieter pressure point nobody warns Year 9 parents about. The subject-choice form goes in before anybody has sat a real IGCSE paper, and it is the decision that constrains everything afterwards. A single session with a tutor who has taught the senior papers, held before the form is submitted, is worth more than a term of remedial work in Year 11. sections.heading: Should a Year 10 student in Dadar Parsi Colony book home classes or online?
paragraphs: Book home classes if you can get them, and the reason here is unusually concrete. Parsi Colony is low-rise and quiet with large old flats, so it is one of the few places in the city where a tutor is working in a genuinely silent room. For a Year 10 student that silence is not a comfort, it is a working condition. A full structured paper worked under timed conditions at a dining table, with nobody passing through and no traffic noise coming in through the window, is a closer rehearsal of an examination hall than most Mumbai homes can offer at any price.

Home tuition also gives the tutor information they cannot get any other way. They see where the child works, what is on the table, whether the syllabus is printed out, how the notes are organised, and whether the past papers in the folder have been marked or just attempted. An IGCSE home tutor in Dadar Parsi Colony typically redesigns the working setup in the first fortnight, and that change alone often moves marks before any new content is taught.

An IGCSE online tutor in Dadar Parsi Colony is the right answer in three situations. A scarce subject where the only strong Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel specialist is not in the island city. A revision phase where sessions are frequent and short and travel time is the dominant cost. And a candidate who is already working independently and needs marking and feedback rather than teaching. Online work for a diagram-heavy or working-heavy subject needs a document camera or a tablet the child can write on, and without that the tutor is guessing at where the method went wrong.

Hybrid is what most families here settle into by the second term, and it is worth planning for rather than drifting into. One home session a week for teaching and diagnosis, one shorter online session for marking a paper the child has already sat. The honest trade-off is that hybrid needs more discipline from the household than a single weekly visit: somebody has to make sure the paper is actually sat before the online slot, or the session becomes a conversation. Online sessions also rescue the evenings when the monsoon shuts the roads, which in Mumbai is not a rare event.

Whether they have a standing commitment that conflicts with your window. Whether they teach the subject at the tier your child is entered for, rather than one tier below it. A tutor comfortable with Core content and uncomfortable with the Extended paper is a poor match for an Extended candidate, however pleasant the first session is.

Then there is the part you do yourself, and it is not optional. On the call, ask the tutor to name the components of the paper your child sits and describe what the examiner wants in each. Ask what they would do in the first session. Ask for one specific thing they changed for a student in the same year group. sections.heading: Why an uninterrupted hour in Parsi Colony is worth more at IGCSE than anywhere else in Mumbai
paragraphs: IGCSE rewards one thing above almost everything else in the final year: the ability to sit a whole paper, at pace, without stopping. Most children in this city have never done it outside an examination hall. They have done questions, sets of questions, homework, chapters. They have not sat down at seven in the evening and worked through a complete structured paper from the first mark to the last while somebody timed it. The reason is almost never motivation. It is that the room will not allow it.

A flat on a main road in this city is not a quiet room at 7pm. Horns, a generator, a lift motor, a neighbour's renovation, the television two rooms away. A child working in that environment learns to work in bursts, because bursts are all the room permits, and bursts are exactly the wrong habit for a two-hour paper. The marks lost are not content marks. They are the marks that go in the last third of the paper, when concentration has already been spent on filtering noise.

Parsi Colony is the exception, and it is worth using deliberately rather than taking for granted. The low-rise blocks, the tree cover around Five Gardens, the absence of a through road carrying evening traffic: the practical result is that a tutor sitting in a large old flat here has a working hour that behaves like an examination hall. A tutor who understands that will structure the term around it. Teaching and diagnosis in the first part of the year, then timed full papers in the room, marked against the mark scheme in front of the child, from the mock series onwards.

The second thing the quiet buys is honest diagnosis. In a noisy room a tutor cannot tell whether a child stopped because they did not know the next step or because they lost the thread. In a silent room that distinction is visible, and it changes the teaching completely: one is a content gap and gets taught, the other is a working-memory and method problem and gets drilled. On what IGCSE tuition fees in Dadar Parsi Colony buy, this is the honest version: the same hourly rate produces more here than in a flat on a main road, because the hour is actually an hour.
bullets: Full timed papers are the habit IGCSE rewards most in Year 11
Noisy rooms teach working in bursts, which costs end-of-paper marks

Silence lets a tutor separate a content gap from a method problem

sections.heading: What four weeks, one term and one series of IGCSE results should show
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at marks. You should be looking at whether the diagnosis was right and whether the child is working differently. Concretely: the tutor has told you which topics are weak and why, in the language of the paper rather than in general terms. The child has sat at least one thing under timed conditions. The folder has changed. There is a written plan with a small number of priorities rather than a promise to cover everything. If none of that has happened in four sessions, the match is not working and you should say so rather than wait.

At one term the marks should have moved somewhere, though not necessarily where you expect. The first visible change is usually in the structured questions, because method and presentation are faster to fix than conceptual gaps. A child who was leaving the last pages of a paper blank starts finishing. A child who was writing the right physics in the wrong command word starts answering what was asked. Overall grade movement often lags behind that by a reporting cycle, which is why the term report can look flat while the underlying work has genuinely improved.

Across a full examination cycle, the realistic picture is that a well-matched tutor plus consistent work from the student moves outcomes meaningfully, and that neither of those two ingredients works alone. We do not guarantee grades and we will not publish a success rate, because the honest determinants are the child's starting point, the time left, the subject, and how much independent work happens between sessions. A tutor who tells you a specific grade is available in four months is telling you what you want to hear.

There are also cases where you should not hire a tutor at all, and we would rather say so. A child who is exhausted and sleeping badly needs the schedule reduced, not another weekly commitment. A child who has not opened the textbook does not have a teaching problem. A child failing across six subjects at once usually has something going on that a subject tutor cannot reach, and the school counsellor is the right first call. Home tuition across Mumbai is useful for a specific, diagnosable, subject-shaped problem, and it is poor value for anything else.
bullets: Week four: a written diagnosis in paper language, not a grade promise
Week four: at least one timed attempt and a reorganised folder
One term: structured questions improve before the headline grade

sections.heading: What to have ready before the first IGCSE home tuition session in Mumbai
paragraphs: Four things, and they take ten minutes to gather. The board and syllabus code for every subject you want help with. The most recent school report or assessment sheet, with the actual mark breakdown rather than the grade. The child's last marked paper, mistakes and all, because the mistakes are the brief. And the two evening windows you can genuinely protect for the next three months, which is a harder question than it sounds in a household with two children and a commute.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like one. Expect the tutor to spend most of it watching your child work rather than talking: a few questions from the weak topic, one short timed section, and a conversation about how the child currently revises. Expect to be told something you did not want to hear. A tutor who comes out of a first session saying everything is fine and the child just needs practice has not done the work. By the end of it you should have a short written list of priorities and a fixed weekly slot.

Practical arrangements are worth settling in the same conversation. The tutor will need to be named at the gate for a standing weekly entry rather than signing in as a new visitor each week, and in the older blocks here that is a two-minute conversation with the watchman that saves ten minutes every session. Decide where the session happens and keep it the same place. Decide whether a parent is in the room, which for Years 9 to 11 is usually better as nearby rather than present. Agree what happens when a session is missed.

If it is not working after three or four sessions, say it early. A replacement match is a normal part of this process and not a complaint: tutor and student fit is partly personality, and nobody gets it right every time. We would rather rematch you in week three than have you quietly stop in week nine with a term gone. Tell us what specifically did not work, because that detail makes the second match better than the first.
bullets: Bring board, syllabus code, report breakdown and one marked paper
Protect two evening windows for three months, not for one week
Expect a diagnostic first session and one uncomfortable finding
Get the tutor named at the gate for standing weekly entry
Ask for a rematch in week three, not in week nine

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE home tutor in Dadar Parsi Colony cost, and what changes the figure?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate, and anybody quoting one before knowing the subject is guessing. The figure moves on five things: the board, because Pearson Edexcel specialists in some subjects are scarcer than Cambridge ones; the year group, since Year 11 final-series work is priced differently from Year 9 foundations; subject scarcity, which is why a Mathematics tutor and an Economics tutor are not comparable; travel, which is why island matching keeps costs sensible here; and session length. Tell us the subject, tier and evening window and you get a real range rather than a headline number designed to get you on a call.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel from Matunga or Sion for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and those two areas are where we look first. Matunga is the next area north and Sion sits beyond it, both a short run from Dadar station, and neither journey crosses the signals that destroy evening timings further south. A tutor already teaching in Matunga on a Tuesday can hold a 7pm Parsi Colony slot for a full term. What we avoid is promising a weekday evening slot to a tutor coming down from the western or eastern suburbs: that arrangement looks fine in September and collapses by November, usually without anybody admitting why.

faqs.question: Our flat is on the third floor of an old low-rise building with no lift. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Not for tutoring, and it is worth mentioning when we match rather than on the first evening. Most of the older blocks in Parsi Colony are walk-ups, tutors here expect that, and nobody has declined a match over three flights. It is worth flagging only if a tutor has a mobility issue, which is a conversation we have at matching rather than at your door. The genuine advantage of these buildings outweighs the stairs: thick walls, high ceilings and no lift motor humming through the wall means the room is quiet in a way newer towers are not.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with the final series four months away. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan has to change shape. Four months is not enough to re-teach a two-year syllabus, and a tutor who says otherwise is selling. What four months does buy is triage: identify the three or four topics carrying the most marks where your child is weakest, fix those properly, and spend the rest on full timed papers marked against the mark scheme. Expect the tutor to refuse to cover everything, and treat that refusal as a good sign. Two sessions a week in this window is usually better than one longer one.

faqs.question: How do you handle a tutor who is not working out after three sessions?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week three and we rematch, with no argument and no requirement to justify it at length. We do ask one thing: describe specifically what did not work. Too fast, too slow, no written plan, no marking, personality mismatch, arrives late. That detail is what makes the second match better rather than a coin toss. Rematching is normal and happens in a meaningful minority of placements, because fit at this age is partly about personality. The expensive mistake is not the wrong first tutor, it is waiting until week ten to say so.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a gate pass each week, or can we arrange standing entry?
faqs.answer: Arrange standing entry in the first week. In the older low-rise blocks here it is a two-minute conversation: give the watchman the tutor's name, the day and the time, and the visitor register entry becomes routine rather than a negotiation. Doing this once saves five to ten minutes at the start of every session, which across a term is close to two full sessions. If your block uses a digital visitor system, add the tutor as a recurring expected visitor. Tutors will not ask for this themselves, so it falls to you.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics taught differently from Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps substantially, the examinations do not, and the difference matters most in the final year. Each board phrases questions differently, structures papers differently and rewards different presentation habits. A student drilled on one board's past papers and then entered for the other arrives with the wrong instincts about how much working to show and what the command words demand. Match the tutor to the board your child is actually entered for, confirm the syllabus code with the school, and check the current syllabus document rather than relying on how the paper looked a few years ago.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Physics and Chemistry at Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and you should ask hard questions before accepting it. Plenty of science graduates can teach both competently at this level, and a single tutor covering two sciences saves a slot and keeps the week manageable. The test is depth in the second subject: ask them to describe the structured and practical components of each, and what students most commonly lose marks on in the one they teach less. If the answer for the second subject is vague, take two tutors. Two strong single-subject matches beat one convenient double match every time.

faqs.question: What if my child is strong in class but loses marks in every mock paper?
faqs.answer: That is a paper-technique problem, not a content problem, and it is the most common brief we receive from Year 10 and Year 11 families. The usual causes are identifiable: not reading the command word, showing too little working to earn method marks, spending too long on early questions and leaving the last pages blank, or quoting answers to the wrong precision. Diagnosis needs a full paper sat under timed conditions and then marked line by line with the child watching. This is exactly the work that benefits from a quiet room, and it moves marks faster than new teaching.

faqs.question: Will online sessions work if our tutor is stuck in Peddar Road traffic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and agreeing that fallback in advance is worth more than it sounds. South Mumbai is short-distance but slow, and the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals can cost forty minutes in the evening peak even on an eight-kilometre run. The arrangement that works is a standing rule: if the tutor is more than twenty minutes out at the start time, the session converts to online for that evening rather than being cancelled. For that to work the child needs a tablet or a document camera so the tutor can see the working, not just the final answer.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Year 9 subject-choice form rather than a specific subject?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the most useful one-off sessions we arrange. A tutor who has taught the senior papers can tell you what each shortlisted subject actually demands in Year 11, which combinations produce clustered coursework deadlines, and whether a Core or Extended entry is realistic in each. That is usually one or two sessions rather than a weekly commitment, and we will say so rather than converting it into a term. Bring the school's option blocks, your child's current marks and the subjects they are genuinely interested in.

faqs.question: What should a parent do during an IGCSE home tuition session at home?
faqs.answer: Be nearby and not in the room, for this age group. A Year 9 to Year 11 student works differently with a parent watching, usually worse, and the tutor loses the honest picture of what the child can do unaided. Being nearby still matters: you want to hear whether teaching is happening or a conversation is happening. Ask for two minutes at the end of each session rather than a weekly report, and ask what the child got wrong rather than how they did. A tutor who cannot name a specific error is not marking closely enough.

sections.heading: How a Dadar IGCSE request becomes a shortlist in four steps
paragraphs: A request for an IGCSE home tutor in Dadar usually arrives with three facts, and we need five before anyone is sent anywhere. Parents tell us the year group, the subject and the area. What decides whether the match survives past week three is the tier the school has already entered the child for, whether the examination series in question is the coming one or the one after it, and what the last report card said about method rather than about marks. A report that says a Year 10 student is careless is useless. A report that says she loses marks because she does not write down the rearrangement step before substituting is a brief.

Once those are on the table, the register is filtered by board and subject before anything else is considered. An IGCSE home tutor in Dadar who teaches Extended Mathematics is not interchangeable with one who teaches Core, and a Cambridge International Education Coordinated Sciences teacher is not a straight swap for someone who has only taught separate Physics, Chemistry and Biology. The second filter is travel, and in South Mumbai travel means minutes rather than kilometres. A tutor living near Matunga or Prabhadevi can hold a half past six slot in Dadar every week of term without renegotiating it. A tutor living in Colaba can reach you once, impressively, and then start asking to move to Sundays.

You then receive two or three profiles, not twenty. Each one states the board taught, the subjects and tiers, how many IGCSE cohorts the tutor has taken through to examinations, and which evenings are genuinely free rather than theoretically free. You choose who to speak to. The first session is paid and diagnostic, and either side can decline afterwards without producing a reason for it.

The reason this works better in Dadar than in most Mumbai addresses is the interchange itself. A tutor who lives in Thane, Bandra, Chembur or Ghatkopar can reach Dadar on one train with no change, which is why tutors accept standing Dadar slots they would turn down three kilometres away across Peddar Road. Your shortlist is therefore deeper here than the map suggests, and you should use that depth on subject fit rather than on proximity.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE tier should a Year 9 student in Dadar be entered for?
paragraphs: Core and Extended are two different papers, two different grade ranges and two different conversations with a Year 11 student in March. Extended reaches the top grades and is what most Dadar families assume their child is on. Core caps the grade available and exists so that a student who would otherwise collapse under algebraic demand can still finish with a usable certificate. The decision is made by the school, usually late in Year 9 or early in Year 10, and most parents only discover it happened when a mock paper comes home that looks easier than they expected.

This is the single most useful thing IGCSE home tuition in Dadar does early. A tutor who sees a Year 9 student in September can tell you within three sessions whether Extended is realistic, and if it is marginal, what specifically has to change for it to stop being marginal. That is almost always algebraic fluency rather than topic coverage. Students who are moved down tiers are rarely short of content knowledge. They are short of the ability to rearrange, factorise and substitute without stopping to think.

Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both run two-tier structures, and they are not identical in feel. Edexcel International GCSE papers tend to signal the required method more explicitly in the question wording; Cambridge papers more often expect the student to choose the method themselves. A tutor who has taught both will tell you which one your child's school actually enters for, because families frequently do not know, and the specification code on the front of a past paper settles it in ten seconds.

One sentence about what comes after, since a sibling page covers it properly: the subjects and tiers chosen now set which Higher Level options remain open in a two-year diploma later, so a Year 9 tier decision is quietly a Year 12 decision too. Ask the subject teacher what the school's own entry policy is before you accept it as fixed.

sections.heading: The eight-subject spread Mumbai IGCSE students actually carry
paragraphs: A typical IGCSE student at a Mumbai international school carries somewhere between seven and nine subjects: a first language, a second language, Mathematics, two or three sciences in some configuration, one humanity, and something from the creative or technical group. The load is wide rather than deep, and that width is what produces the particular IGCSE failure mode. A student does not fall behind in one subject. She falls behind in whichever subject had coursework due in the same fortnight as two others.

Several IGCSE subjects carry an internally assessed or coursework component that is marked in school and moderated by the board. Sciences carry practical skills that are assessed either through an alternative-to-practical paper or through a laboratory component, depending on what the school has chosen. Languages carry speaking and listening work. Art and Design carries a sustained portfolio that eats weekends in a way no parent anticipates. These pieces are the part of the certificate most within reach of a tutor, because they are produced over weeks rather than in one examination hall, and a tutor can see drafts.

When families ask us for a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai, we say the honest thing: nobody teaches all of them well. What we can do is cover a student's whole spread with two or three tutors rather than one, usually a Mathematics and science specialist, a humanities and English specialist, and a language teacher if a second language is the weak point. Running three tutors sounds expensive and often is not, because each one needs fewer sessions than a single generalist would.

The practical rule we give Dadar parents is to tutor the subject where the method is learnable, not the subject where the marks are lowest. Mathematics, the sciences and languages respond quickly to structured work. A student who dislikes History will usually not start enjoying it, but she can be taught to write a source-comparison paragraph that scores, and that is a different and more achievable goal.

sections.heading: What the school calendar in Mumbai does to a Year 11 term
paragraphs: Families in and around Dadar send children to a handful of international schools within reasonable reach, and the two that come up most often on our calls are Don Bosco International School in Matunga and JBCN International School, Parel, a short drive down towards Lower Parel. Both run international pathways, and both set the rhythm that a tutor has to work inside. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Don Bosco International School, JBCN International School, Parel, or any other school named anywhere on this page. We name them because they are where these children actually go, and because their calendars are the reason certain weeks are impossible.

The IGCSE year in Mumbai has predictable pressure points. The first comes in late October and early November, when first-term examinations land and coursework deadlines cluster behind them. The second is January and early February, when Year 11 mocks arrive and the gap between a predicted grade and a real one becomes visible to everyone at once. The third is the stretch from late February into the written examination series, when there is nothing left to teach and everything left to practise.

That pattern decides when starting home classes in Mumbai is useful and when it is late. A student who begins in June or July has a full run at the subject. One who begins in September is in good time. One who begins the week after January mocks is not too late, but the work changes shape completely: no new content, a triage of the two or three topics that are costing the most marks, and a lot of timed paper practice under conditions that resemble the real hall.

Mumbai schools also run their own internal moderation and portfolio deadlines, and these rarely appear on the family calendar until a Sunday evening panic. Ask your child in September to show you every coursework deadline for the year in one list. Most cannot produce it. Building that list is often the first hour of useful tutoring anyone does.

sections.heading: Home classes, online or both for an IGCSE student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home is the default and should be, for one reason: a tutor sitting at your dining table sees the exercise book. Everything useful about diagnosing an IGCSE student is in the working rather than in the answer, and a student who has learned to narrate her method out loud over a video call while hiding a page of crossed-out attempts is very good at appearing to understand. IGCSE home classes in Dadar work particularly well because the slot holds: a tutor arriving by train at the interchange is not fighting the Coastal Road or the Western Line crush at a bad hour.

Online is the right answer in three specific situations and the wrong answer otherwise. It is right for a scarce subject, where the only competent Economics or Computer Science teacher for your board does not live in South Mumbai at all. It is right for short, frequent contact during a revision run, where three half-hour sessions a week beat one long one. And it is right in the monsoon, when a Thursday session that would otherwise be cancelled can simply move to a screen. An IGCSE online tutor in Dadar is a real option rather than a fallback, and for a Year 11 doing past papers it is often the better one.

Hybrid is what most of our Dadar families settle into by the second term without planning it. One longer session at home each week for new material and marking, and one short online session for a paper walkthrough or a doubt-clearing slot before a test. It costs less than two home sessions and gives more contact than one.

The honest trade-off nobody mentions: an IGCSE private tutor in Dadar who comes to your flat charges for the travel whether or not it appears as a line item, and in Mumbai, Maharashtra that travel is the most expensive hour of the arrangement. Online removes it. Home buys you something the screen cannot replicate, which is a stranger in the room noticing that your child cannot do long division without a calculator.
bullets: Home sessions let a tutor read the working, not only the answer
Online suits scarce subjects and short, frequent revision contact

sections.heading: How are IGCSE home tutors in Dadar checked before you meet them?
paragraphs: Before a tutor appears on a shortlist we confirm three things: identity, through government photo identification; qualification, through the actual degree certificate rather than a claim on a profile; and board experience, through a conversation with someone who can tell the difference between having taught a syllabus and having taught a specification. An IGCSE home tutor in Dadar, Mumbai who says they teach IGCSE and cannot name which board's papers they have marked or worked through is not put in front of a family.

What we cannot do is verify teaching quality from paperwork, and we do not pretend otherwise. A degree in Chemistry proves someone knows chemistry. It proves nothing about whether a fifteen year old will understand her moles calculation an hour later. That part is yours to assess, and the diagnostic session exists so that you can.

Here is what to check yourself in that first hour. Ask the tutor which board and which paper numbers your child sits, and watch whether the answer is specific. Ask what they will do differently for Extended than for Core. Ask them to name one topic they expect your child to be weak on before they have seen any work, and then see whether they were right. Ask how they will tell you about progress and how often. A tutor who answers all four crisply is usually worth a term.

Two warning signs are worth more than any certificate. The first is a tutor who talks about results in aggregate rather than about your child's specific gaps. The second is anyone who promises a particular grade. No honest tutor offers a guaranteed grade, because the variables sitting outside a two-hour weekly session are too large. IB Gram does not guarantee grades either, and any page that tells you otherwise is selling something. What we guarantee is that the tutor is who they say they are and teaches the board you need.

Board experience confirmed in conversation, not from a profile claim

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition fees in Dadar actually depend on
paragraphs: We do not publish a rate card, because a single number would be wrong for most of the people reading it. IGCSE tuition fees in Dadar depend on five things, and once you know them you can tell whether a quote you have been given is reasonable without anyone naming a figure. The first is subject scarcity. Mathematics and the three sciences have a deep pool of competent teachers in South Mumbai. Economics, Business Studies, Computer Science, Art and Design and any second language other than Hindi, French or Spanish have a thin one, and thin pools cost more regardless of difficulty.

The second is tier and year group. A Year 9 student starting early is cheaper per session than a Year 11 student eight weeks from written papers, because the second is urgent and urgency is priced. The third is travel, and this is where the Dadar interchange genuinely saves money. A tutor who reaches you on one train without changing lines does not need the premium that a tutor crossing the island at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak will quite reasonably ask for. The best IGCSE tutor in Dadar for your child may well be cheaper than a weaker one in a harder-to-reach address, purely because of the journey.

The fourth is session length and frequency. Two ninety-minute sessions a week is a different arrangement from one three-hour marathon, and the longer single session is usually worse value because attention does not hold. The fifth is whether the tutor is handling coursework. Reading and commenting on drafts between sessions is real unpaid work if it is not priced in, and a tutor who does it for free will stop doing it by November.

What to ask on the call: whether the rate changes closer to examinations, whether marked work between sessions is included, what happens to the fee if you miss a session with notice, and whether there is a different rate for a second sibling at the same address. Those four answers tell you more about how an arrangement will actually run than the headline number does.

sections.heading: What four weeks of IGCSE home tuition should visibly change
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at a grade. You should be looking at four specific things, and if you cannot see them, something is wrong with the match rather than with your child. First, the tutor can describe your child's weak topics more precisely than the school report did. Second, your child can say what she is currently working on without consulting a notebook. Third, the exercise book shows worked solutions with method lines rather than bare answers. Fourth, homework set by the tutor is being done without a fight on at least most weeks.

At one term, roughly twelve to fourteen sessions, expect a measurable shift in one or two topic areas and a visible shift in exam technique. Students usually gain marks first from stopping avoidable losses: showing method, reading the command word, finishing the paper. Content gains come later and more slowly. A student who was leaving the last two questions blank and now attempts them has gained more than the mark sheet shows, because the habit is what compounds.

At one examination cycle the picture is honest and sometimes uncomfortable. Some students move two grades. Some move one. Some hold a grade they were going to lose, which is a real outcome that looks like nothing happened. We do not guarantee grades, we do not publish success rates, and we will not tell you on a first call what your child will get, because anyone who does is guessing with your money.

What should worry you is stasis in the tutor's language. If at week six the tutor is still saying the same general things about confidence and effort, they are not diagnosing. Ask for the three topics being worked on and what the evidence of improvement is. A good tutor has that answer ready. A tutor who does not is usually filling time politely, and a replacement is a short conversation rather than a confrontation.

sections.heading: Starting IGCSE home classes in Dadar this month
paragraphs: To get a useful shortlist rather than a generic one, have four things ready before you write to us. The year group and the examination series your child is sitting. The board, which you can confirm from the specification code on any past paper the school has issued. The most recent report card or mock script, ideally the script rather than the grade, because the script shows where marks went. And two or three evening windows that genuinely work for your household, not the ones you wish worked.

The first session is diagnostic and is paid at the normal rate. It is not a sales call and it is not a free trial. The tutor spends it on a short written diagnostic, usually past paper questions chosen across topics rather than a single chapter test, and the point is to watch how your child works rather than to score her. Expect the tutor to interrupt, to ask her to explain a step, and to leave with two or three specific topics identified and a plan for the first month.

After that session you get a short written note: what was found, what the first four weeks will cover, and what homework volume to expect between sessions. If you do not want to continue, say so and nothing further happens. If the tutor is not right after two or three weeks, tell us and we re-match from the same shortlist, usually within a week because the Dadar catchment is deep.

One practical request for the first visit. Clear a table with a chair on each side, in a room with a door, and keep the television and the younger sibling out of earshot for the duration. The dining table at seven in the evening in a Mumbai flat is a contested space, and the single biggest avoidable cause of a failed arrangement is that nobody decided in advance where the sessions would happen.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects can you cover in Dadar and Matunga?
faqs.answer: Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Coordinated Sciences, English as a First Language, English as a Second Language, Economics, Business Studies, Accounting, Computer Science, Geography, History, Hindi, French and Spanish are the subjects we are asked for most in Dadar and Matunga, and the pool is deep for the first six. faqs.question: My daughter is in Year 11 with mocks in January. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: No, but the work has to change shape. With mocks weeks away there is no value in starting at chapter one. A tutor should spend the first session triaging: which two or three topics are costing the most marks across recent papers, and which of those can be fixed in the time available. Expect timed paper practice rather than teaching, expect the tutor to mark against the board's own mark scheme, and expect the focus to be on avoidable losses first. Students in this position usually gain fastest from technique and finishing the paper, not from new content.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home while the session runs?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but be at home for the first one. You want to see how the tutor opens, whether your child talks or goes silent, and whether the room you have chosen actually works. After that, most families are comfortable leaving the two of them to it, with a parent or grandparent somewhere in the flat. For a younger IGCSE student in Year 9 we suggest staying within earshot for the first fortnight. For a Year 11 preparing for written papers, a parent hovering is usually counterproductive and the student will tell you so.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three weeks?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we re-match, usually from the same shortlist you already saw. Three weeks is enough to judge fit and not long enough to have lost a term. You do not need to justify the decision or have a confrontation with the tutor; we handle that conversation. What helps is one specific sentence about what went wrong, because the fix is different depending on whether the problem was subject depth, pace, personality or punctuality. Re-matching in Dadar is faster than in most Mumbai localities because the interchange keeps the available pool unusually wide.

faqs.question: Does online IGCSE tuition work as well as home classes in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: For revision and scarce subjects, yes. For diagnosis and for younger students, no. The reason is simple: a tutor at your table reads the working in the exercise book, including the crossed-out attempts, and that is where the real information about an IGCSE student sits. Online, a student can narrate confidently while her page says something else. Where online wins outright is frequency and reliability: three short sessions a week during a revision run, or a monsoon Thursday that would otherwise be cancelled. Most Mumbai families end up running both without planning to.

faqs.question: How do you check an IGCSE tutor before sending them to my building?
faqs.answer: Identity through government photo identification, qualification through the original degree certificate rather than a profile claim, and board experience through a conversation specific enough to separate someone who has taught the specification from someone who has read it. We also confirm the tutor can actually hold the slot and area before the profile reaches you. What we cannot verify from documents is teaching quality, which is why the first session is diagnostic and why you should treat it as an assessment of the tutor as much as of your child.

faqs.question: Should my son be entered for Core or Extended?
faqs.answer: That decision belongs to the school, and the useful question is whether you agree with it. Extended reaches the top grades; Core caps them and exists for students who would otherwise be overwhelmed. If your son is marginal, the deciding factor is almost always algebraic fluency rather than topic coverage. A tutor who sees him three times can tell you specifically what would have to improve for Extended to be safe, and you can then take that to the subject teacher. Ask the school how late a tier change can still be made administratively, because the window closes earlier than most parents expect.

faqs.question: What does progress look like after one term of IGCSE home tuition?
faqs.answer: After twelve to fourteen sessions you should see a measurable shift in one or two topic areas and a clear shift in examination technique. Marks usually arrive first from stopping avoidable losses: showing method, reading the command word, attempting every question. Content gains come later. The tutor should be able to name the three topics currently being worked on and show you the evidence. We do not guarantee grades and we do not publish success rates, because the honest range of outcomes across students is too wide for an average to mean anything useful to you.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Mathematics and Physics for a Year 10 in Prabhadevi?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and in Prabhadevi it is worth asking, because a tutor who already travels for one subject will take the second cheaply. Mathematics and Physics pair well at IGCSE level: the algebra that limits a Physics student is usually the same algebra limiting the Mathematics grade, and one tutor fixing it once is more efficient than two working around it. Chemistry and Biology pair less naturally with Mathematics. Where a student needs three sciences plus Mathematics, two tutors splitting the load usually works better than one carrying all four.

sections.heading: From your message to a verified IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar
paragraphs: The first thing we do with an enquiry is establish which board the school has entered your child with. An IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar who has spent five years on Cambridge papers is not interchangeable with one who knows Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, because the syllabus content overlaps but the paper structures, the command-word habits and the coursework rules do not. Roughly half the parents who write to us do not know which board their child sits, and that is not a criticism: schools rarely put it on the report. A photograph of the front page of a past internal paper settles it in thirty seconds.

Second, the tier. Several Cambridge subjects split into Core and Extended, and the entry decision is sometimes made by the school in Year 10 rather than by the family. A student being prepared on Core content cannot be tutored out of a tier they have already been entered for in the weeks before the series, so this question has a deadline attached to it. If a tier change is still possible and worth arguing for, the tutor's first job is to produce evidence the subject teacher will accept, not to start revision.

Only then do we look at people. We filter for tutors who have actually taught Years 9 to 11 on your board, who live or already teach north of Kandivali, and whose free slot overlaps with yours. The order matters: board, then tier, then level, then geography, then time. Families who skip to geography get a nearby tutor who is strong on a different syllabus, which shows up in week four when the practice questions do not look like the ones in school.

The last step is the part nobody rushes. You speak to the shortlisted tutors yourself before any lesson is booked, and we ask you to put your child on that call for two minutes. IGCSE home tuition in Dahisar lives or dies on whether a fifteen-year-old will talk honestly to this adult about what they do not understand. sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: which board is your child entered with?
paragraphs: Two boards dominate IGCSE in Mumbai: Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel, and your school has chosen one of them for each subject. Cambridge subjects carry four-digit syllabus codes, Edexcel International GCSE subjects carry their own code format, and a syllabus code written at the top of a practice paper is the single most useful piece of information you can send a tutor. The content looks similar from a distance. The question styles, the mark allocations and the way practical science is assessed are not.

Within Cambridge, several subjects are tiered into Core and Extended. Extended covers additional content and opens the upper part of the grade range; Core is a narrower syllabus with a lower ceiling. The exact grade range available on each tier is set out in the current syllabus document, which the board revises on its own schedule, so read it with your subject teacher rather than relying on what a cousin's school did two years ago. What is consistent is the consequence: a Core entry in mathematics narrows which Diploma Programme mathematics route a school will let a student take afterwards.

Edexcel runs its International GCSE without the Core and Extended split in most subjects, which parents often read as simpler. In practice it shifts the difficulty elsewhere, into longer structured questions and, in several subjects, into a different balance between papers. A student moving from a Cambridge school in Kandivali to an Edexcel school in Borivali in Year 10 is the hardest case we see, because their notes, their past-paper library and their exam technique are all calibrated to the wrong format.

Grading scales are the third thing to pin down. Depending on the board and the subject, a certificate may report on a letter scale or a numbered one, and schools in the Western Suburbs use both. Ask the school which scale the certificate for each subject will use before you interpret a mock result, because a parent reading a numbered grade against a letter-scale expectation will either panic or relax for no reason at all.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and the subjects on the table in Year 9
paragraphs: Year 9 is when the subject basket is built, and it is built with less information than the decision deserves. A student typically carries a first language, mathematics, two or three sciences in some combination, a humanity, a second language and an option that may be art, business, computer science or economics. Each one brings its own paper pattern, and a few bring coursework or a practical component that has to be produced during term rather than revised for at the end.

The sciences are where tier and format bite hardest. Separate sciences and the combined route are different commitments, and in several syllabuses the practical skills are assessed through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than in a laboratory. Students who are excellent in the lab and careless about recording data lose marks in exactly the place nobody practises. A tutor who sets a data-table question and marks the units, the significant figures and the axes before touching the explanation is doing the right work.

English and the second language deserve more attention than they get. A student who speaks fluent English at home can still lose a grade on directed writing because they never learned to hold a register, and a student who chose a second language on the basis of family familiarity can find themselves writing formal prose in it for the first time in Year 10. These are the subjects where parents are most surprised by the mock result, because conversational fluency and examined literacy are not the same skill.

When a family asks what all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Dahisar can realistically cover, the honest division is this: one good tutor can carry mathematics plus one science, or two humanities, or a language plus study technique. Three sciences and two languages is four tutors and five evenings, and no fifteen-year-old in Mumbai has five free evenings. Sequence the help. Fix the subject that is costing the most marks now, then move the slot to the next one, and keep the home classes in Mumbai to a load your child can actually absorb.

Schools in the Western Suburbs run a June-start year, which puts Year 9 settling into a new syllabus between June and September, internal assessments and reports through the winter, Year 11 mocks in the cold months, and the examination series itself in the spring. sections.heading: Should Year 10 home classes happen in person or on a screen?
paragraphs: In person, for almost every Year 10 student, and the reason is handwriting. Examined IGCSE work is produced with a pen under time pressure, and a tutor in the room can see that your child is writing the answer before they have read the second half of the question. On a screen, a tutor sees a finished photograph of the work and has to reconstruct what happened. An IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar watching a student attempt a structured question live will catch a habit in one session that would take a month to infer from scans.

Online earns its place in three specific slots. Paper marking turnaround is the first: a student who sits a timed paper on Saturday and gets it marked on a call on Sunday learns more than one who waits for Tuesday's visit. Scarce subjects are the second, and in the north of Mumbai that means the less common languages, business and computer science, where the right specialist may simply not be reachable from the Western Express Highway. The third is the fortnight before a paper, when short, frequent, question-level contact beats a long session.

An IGCSE online tutor in Dahisar is the wrong choice for a Year 9 student who has not yet learned to work alone, and it is the wrong choice when the underlying problem is an unopened folder. We say this to parents who ask for online specifically to save travel time: if the tutoring is partly about building the habit of sitting down and starting, the habit needs a witness. It is also the wrong choice for a student who has already learned that a muted camera is a place to hide.

The arrangement most Year 11 families in this part of Mumbai end up with is mixed by necessity. One visit for teaching, one screen call for marked work, and a willingness to flip a visit to a call during the monsoon, when the highway near Dahisar can double a journey without warning. Set that expectation at the start. A tutor who treats a rained-off visit as a cancelled lesson rather than a screen session is costing you a week every time it pours.

sections.heading: How are IGCSE tutors in Mumbai checked, and what should you check?
paragraphs: We verify identity, the qualification a tutor claims, the boards and year groups they have actually taught, and a contactable reference where one exists. For IGCSE specifically we ask a harder question than for other levels: have you marked work against this board's mark scheme, or only taught the content? A graduate who knows the physics and has never seen how marks are awarded for a six-mark explanation will teach your child to write answers that are correct and underscored. Every IGCSE home tutor in Dahisar we put forward has answered that question before you ever see the profile.

Your own checks should be practical and short. Ask the tutor which syllabus code they last taught and what the paper pattern is; a specialist answers without pausing. Ask what they would do in session one, and be unimpressed by an answer that begins with teaching. Ask how they will show you progress, and listen for something you can see rather than something you have to be told. If you are weighing up an IGCSE private tutor Dahisar neighbours already use, ask them which board that family's school follows before you take the recommendation as transferable.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, who quotes a pass percentage, or who implies any official standing with a school or board. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching service with no affiliation to Singapore International School, JBCN International School, Borivali, Cambridge International Education, Pearson Edexcel or the International Baccalaureate Organization, and we do not guarantee grades. A tutor who promises a specific number has told you something about their sales process, not their teaching.

Parents looking for the best IGCSE tutor in Dahisar usually mean the most reliable one, and reliability is measurable in a way that brilliance is not. Did the lesson happen at the agreed time for four consecutive weeks? Did marked work come back? Can the student name their weakest skill more precisely than a month ago? Those three questions separate good tutors from impressive ones, and they can be answered with evidence by the end of the first month.

sections.heading: The Year 11 result that decides which Diploma subjects stay open
paragraphs: The real stake in Years 9 to 11 is not the certificate; it is which subjects a school will allow at the next stage. Most international schools in the Western Suburbs set entry expectations for continuing into a two-year sixth form, and mathematics and the sciences carry the firmest ones. A student who finishes the Extended tier comfortably keeps every route open. A student on the Core tier, or one who scrapes a science, finds that the conversation in Year 11 is about what they are permitted to take rather than what they want to take.

This is why February of Year 10 is a more important month than most parents realise. A tier change, a subject swap or a serious intervention is still possible then; by the same month in Year 11 it is not. The families we see with the least stressful Year 11 are the ones who read the Year 10 report as a forecast rather than a verdict and acted on the weakest subject while there was still a full year of teaching left.

What does intervention actually look like at this stage? Not more topics. A tutor should pull the last three assessments, mark them again against the real scheme, and sort the lost marks into three piles: content not known, content known but question misread, and content known and question read but answer badly structured. The three piles need different treatment, and the second and third are usually larger than parents expect. A student who loses a quarter of their marks to misread questions does not need more teaching; they need to be made to annotate the question before writing, every time, until it becomes involuntary. Useful home tuition in Mumbai spends its first fortnight on that sorting rather than on fresh content.

Cost follows the same logic, so here is what it depends on rather than a price list. IGCSE tuition fees in Dahisar track the board and tier, how scarce the specialism is, the distance and hour the tutor travels, the length and frequency of sessions, and whether you want weekly teaching or intensive pre-series support. Extended tier sciences and the uncommon languages sit at the top because fewer people can teach them properly; a Year 9 mathematics slot fifteen minutes away sits at the bottom. The request behind this page is in practice an all IB and IGCSE subjects IGCSE Years 9-11 tutor Mumbai search, and the price only becomes real once you narrow it to one subject, one tier and one slot.

sections.heading: Four weeks, one term, one series: what should actually change
paragraphs: In the first four weeks, the thing to watch is the student's vocabulary about their own work. A Year 10 student who moves from 'I am bad at chemistry' to 'I lose marks when a question says suggest because I describe instead' has made the only kind of progress that compounds. Alongside that, you should be able to see marked work with the scheme's language on it, and the tutor should be able to say what next week targets without looking anything up. No test score is required for this judgement, and demanding one in week four produces teaching to the wrong thing.

Over one term, expect one or two narrow skills to be genuinely fixed. Data tables recorded correctly. Structured questions answered in the order the marks are allocated. An essay plan that exists before the first sentence. A term is also long enough to clear a specific content gap, like the trigonometry that was missed during a school change. It is not long enough to rebuild three years of arithmetic weakness, and a tutor who tells you in week two that it is has not looked at the exercise books.

Across a full examination series the useful comparison is mock to final, not report to certificate. The students who move most between those two points are usually the ones whose technique was the problem rather than their knowledge, because technique responds fast. Students with real content gaps move more slowly and sometimes less than their effort deserves, which is unfair and true. We do not guarantee grades, we publish no success rates, and we will tell you in the first month if we think the timeline you are hoping for is not available.

What we do commit to is the review. At two to four weeks we ask you three questions and ask the tutor one: what is this student's weakest skill, and what did you do about it this week. If the answers from the two sides do not resemble each other, the match is wrong and we replace the tutor without an argument and without a fee for the change. There is no lock-in, so the only thing keeping an engagement alive should be that it is working. The home classes we arrange in Mumbai continue on that basis and on nothing else.

sections.heading: Booking IGCSE home tuition in Dahisar before the next series
paragraphs: Three things make the first message useful: the board and syllabus code if you have it, a photograph of the most recent marked assessment, and the slot you can protect every week for a term. The marked assessment is the most valuable of the three. A tutor reading a real script with a teacher's comments on it can tell you within ten minutes whether the problem is content, reading or structure, and that judgement decides who we put in front of you.

The first session should feel more like an examination than a lesson. A good tutor will set questions from your child's actual syllabus at slightly above current performance, watch where the pen stops, and mark the attempt out loud so the student hears how marks are awarded. By the end of it there should be a written target for the week, specific enough that you could check it yourself. If the first session was a tour of the syllabus, ask for a different tutor.

Choose the slot first. In Dahisar the slots that survive a full term are weekday evenings from about 7pm, once the Western Express Highway has thinned, and Saturday mornings, which are the most contested hours in the Western Suburbs. faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on Cambridge or Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Look at the top of any school practice paper or past internal assessment: the board name and a syllabus code are almost always printed there. Failing that, email the subject teacher and ask for the syllabus code, which is the precise thing a tutor needs. Schools in the Western Suburbs sometimes use Cambridge International Education for the sciences and Pearson Edexcel for a language, or the reverse, so check it subject by subject rather than assuming one board covers the whole timetable. faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Dahisar East on a weekday evening in exam season?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is based in the north, and that is exactly who we shortlist. The practical catchment is Dahisar, Borivali East, Borivali West, Kandivali and Mira Road, and Metro Lines 2A and 7 have widened it as far south as Malad and Goregaon. faqs.question: Can the tutor use our building's study room instead of coming into the flat?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and in some buildings it works better. A society study room or a quiet corner of the clubhouse removes the television, the doorbell and the younger sibling, which are the three most common reasons a session loses twenty minutes. Check the booking rules at your society office first, because many buildings near Dahisar station require a resident to reserve the room and some do not allow non-residents in without a pass. faqs.question: What should I tell the society gate about a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Give the gate the tutor's full name and mobile number and ask the society office to register them as a recurring weekly visitor rather than issuing a fresh pass each time. This takes one conversation and saves an argument every week, particularly in buildings that tighten entry rules during examination months. The tutor should carry photo identification to every session regardless of what the register says, and if your building requires an ID copy in advance we can ask the tutor to send it straight to you.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 9 and the first report is poor. Is it too early for a tutor?
faqs.answer: It is the best time, not too early. Year 9 reports are the cheapest diagnosis you will ever get, because there is a full teaching runway left and no entry decision has hardened yet. A tutor working in September of Year 9 can fix how a student reads a question and records data, and those two habits pay back in every subject for the next three years. By comparison, a tutor hired in February of Year 11 is doing triage, choosing which lost marks are recoverable in the time available.

faqs.question: Should we push the school to move our child to the Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence, and only while there is still time. Ask the subject teacher what specifically would need to improve, then have a tutor produce marked work at Extended standard over four to six weeks and take that to the school. Schools are reasonable when shown current work and resistant when shown ambition. If the entry has already been made for the coming series, accept it and aim high within the tier, because preparing for content your child is not entered for wastes the months that matter.

faqs.question: Is one tutor enough for three sciences?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the realistic answer depends on the route. On a combined science course, one capable tutor can usually carry the whole subject because the depth in each discipline is bounded. On separate sciences at Extended tier, two tutors is the honest minimum and three is common, because the practical and data-handling conventions differ. What works in Dahisar is sequencing rather than stacking: fix the weakest science for a term, then switch the slot. Two tutors sharing a single evening of home tuition in Dahisar is far easier to sustain than four spread across the week, which produces a tired student and no visible gain.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Dahisar actually depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and tier, how scarce the subject specialism is, how far and at what hour the tutor travels, session length and frequency, and whether you need steady weekly teaching or intensive support close to a series. We publish no price list because any figure here would be wrong for somebody: an Extended tier physics specialist coming from Borivali at 8pm is a different cost from a Year 9 mathematics tutor ten minutes away on a Saturday morning. Send your actual brief and ask for a number against it.

faqs.question: The tutor is pleasant but nothing is improving. What do we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for a replacement, and ask us this week rather than at the end of term. Before we change anyone we check three things: whether the sessions actually happened weekly, whether marked work exists, and whether your child can describe their weakness more precisely than a month ago. If sessions kept moving, the schedule is the problem and a new tutor will hit the same wall. If the sessions happened and there is nothing to show, the match is wrong. Replacement costs nothing and keeps your slot.

faqs.question: Do you have tutors who know JBCN International School, Borivali and Singapore International School?
faqs.answer: Some of our tutors have worked with students from both, and that familiarity is useful for one practical reason: they know the assessment rhythm and how the reports are worded, which shortens the first session. It is not a relationship. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with JBCN International School, Borivali, Singapore International School, or any examination board.
